Impl/02 §2.8 represents tuple types and values as ordered HIR arrays and erases grouping parentheses, so only a trailing-comma one-tuple has tuple shape. Checking supported fields against an expected tuple type extends the existing direct-literal checker without adding inference or const evaluation. Arity diagnostics take precedence because fields cannot be paired when lengths differ. Without an expected tuple type, interpreting scalar literals inside a tuple requires additional inference, so the reverse-shape case remains behind the feature gate. Unit fields reuse the exact empty-tuple representation already covered by IR-727. Byte strings remain gated because their type is `Slice<Byte>`, whose checking is Stage 2 (spec/16 §16.1.6).
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver const_flat_tuple_literal_check_accepts_only_supported_direct_fields --locked` passes. `cargo test -p sai_cli --test check_empty_source --locked` passes all 25 tests. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Regressions cover multi-field and single-field tuples, canonical `Str` and unit fields, grouping versus tuple HIR shape, field type and range errors, zero/short/long arity, source-ordered multiple diagnostics with exact literal spans, success-result suppression, reverse-shape gating, and nested/array/expression/alias gates.

The review's suggested coverage for multiple field errors and reverse-shape gating was added; field-level tests also pin diagnostic spans. **Review required:** Confirm that accepting only one nonempty tuple level with supported scalar/unit leaves is an appropriate intermediate boundary; that arity mismatch produces one tuple-level diagnostic before field checks; and that nonempty tuple values against scalar/unit types stay gated until tuple inference is available.

### IR-729: check a direct function-parameter tail

- **Decision:** Add a narrow function-body check for exactly one public, attribute-free, safe, synchronous, non-generic function with one named immutable parameter and no `where`, `borrows`, `effects`, `requires`, or `ensures` clauses. The body must be a statement-free block whose tail is a plain path resolving by `BindingId` to that parameter. The parameter and return types must resolve to a supported primitive or unit type; an omitted return type means unit. Equal types pass; when the expected type is unit, the supported tail value is discarded; otherwise a mismatch reports one `TYPE_MISMATCH` at the tail. Independently, diagnose non-ASCII names on active `pub`/`export` items, `pub` fields, variants and fields of `pub` enums, public trait items, inherent `pub` methods, interfaces/worlds and all locally declared WIT names (including function parameters), and active public re-export aliases. Check trait-impl member names at their trait declaration to avoid duplicates, and do not diagnose declarations removed by the selected target. Non-ASCII parameter names outside interfaces/worlds and unnecessary raw identifiers remain gated. Keep `Str`, aliases, mutable parameters, names that could trigger `NAMING_CONVENTION`, every attribute or clause, every other expression, and all other source shapes behind the feature gate.
- **Reason:** Stage 0 includes type checking non-generic programs (spec/05 §5.20); a function body's tail is checked against the declared result type (spec/06 §§6.1.3 and 6.11.1), unequal types report `TYPE_MISMATCH` (spec/06 §6.1.2), and a non-unit value at an expected-unit tail is discarded (spec/06 §6.11.1). Spec/02 §2.4 requires `NON_ASCII_PUBLIC_NAME` for non-ASCII public names. Phase 1 owner descriptors preserve active target filtering and let the pass inspect declaration syntax without coupling it to the direct-body check. `pub` fields are checked even when their parent record/resource is private because the spec lists them independently; interface/world function parameters are checked because they become WIT names; trait-impl methods are excluded because the trait owns their names. A non-function `export` marker is treated as public during parser recovery, so the public-name diagnostic can accompany the invalid-target diagnostic. The pass does not make an otherwise unsupported body or package shape checkable; `FEATURE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` may appear alongside the hard error. The current repository does not yet implement the planned general `typeck(owner)` query or `TypeckResults`. Reusing resolved HIR bindings and primitive paths checks the direct parameter tail without comparing source spellings or claiming general inference. `Str` remains gated because view/region handling is outside this check. Mutable parameters remain gated because the default `UNNECESSARY_VAR` pass is not implemented. Non-ASCII parameter names outside interfaces/worlds remain gated because the `NON_ASCII_IDENTIFIER` lint pass is not implemented; names containing uppercase characters remain gated because the default `NAMING_CONVENTION` lint pass is not implemented. Raw identifier spellings remain gated so the slice cannot suppress `UNNECESSARY_RAW_IDENT`.
- **Verification:** The focused driver regression checks the direct identity body, a precise return-type mismatch span/message, unit-return discard behavior for omitted and explicit `-> ()`, and gates for operators, `Str`, mutable parameters, recovered `self` parameters, naming conventions, non-ASCII parameters, and unnecessary raw identifiers in function names, parameters, body paths, and type paths; it passes. CLI integration checks success, mismatch result suppression, exact non-ASCII function-name span, reporting through `@inline`, `export` functions including parser-recovered non-function exports, public trait methods and associated types, public fields and enum variants, interface/world names and function parameters, active public re-exports, extra source modules, and exclusion of a target-filtered declaration. It also checks continued gating for expression statements, generics, private functions, lint-producing names/parameters, unnecessary raw identifiers (including a const type), `Str`, multiple declarations, and other unsupported source shapes. All 37 focused CLI tests pass. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Review:** Hostile review found P2 risks that the new result path could suppress default `NAMING_CONVENTION`, `UNNECESSARY_VAR`, and non-ASCII identifier diagnostics; the checker now gates those cases. Follow-up reviews found the public-name hard diagnostic was not reachable through the body checker and that a raw-source scan would miss `export`, public members, dependencies, and target filtering. Review also caught trait-impl duplicate reports and non-function `export` recovery; the final design restricts impl-member checks to inherent impls and treats a recovered `export` marker as public for a declaration and its inherited trait members. The pass walks active Phase 1 owner descriptors for every complete source package, resolves each descriptor into the current snapshot's syntax tree, and checks public fields, public trait members, interface/world names including function parameters, and active public re-exports. It does not suppress the feature gate, and a target-filtered declaration contributes no name diagnostic. The raw-identifier guard also prevents the new success slice from suppressing `UNNECESSARY_RAW_IDENT` and closes the same bypass in the existing const type shortcut. Independent driver review found that a supported non-unit tail is discarded for an expected-unit function rather than reported as a mismatch; the implementation and tests now follow that rule. The same review confirmed recovered `self` parameters are excluded by the HIR path-root check, and an explicit `is_self` guard keeps that boundary fail-closed. Two independent hostile CLI reviews confirmed the export recovery, inherent-impl restriction, WIT parameter and public-field coverage, target filtering, and spans with no remaining P0–P2 findings. **Review required:** Confirm the direct-tail boundary; unit-return discard behavior; default-lint and raw-identifier behavior; public-name visibility rules and coexistence of `NON_ASCII_PUBLIC_NAME` with parser/feature-gate errors; exclusion of trait-impl members and inclusion of inherent methods; WIT parameter names and public fields of private records; exclusion of `Str` and other view types; exact binding-based parameter identification; and result suppression on type mismatch.
- **Remaining scope:** General function-body type checking, expression forms beyond the direct parameter tail and the later zero-parameter scalar-literal tail, local statements, aliases, tuple and record types, `Str` and borrow regions, inference, generic programs, lint analysis and fixes, test analysis, WIT/artifact analysis, and general Stage 0 conformance remain incomplete.

### IR-750: extract the scalar primitive-literal semantic kernel

- **Decision:** Add a pure semantic kernel in `sai_ty::typeck::literal`, `check_primitive_literal(expected, literal, symbols, pointer_width)`, for exact `Bool`, `Char`, `Byte`, integer, and `F32`/`F64` literal/type compatibility. Return `Match`, `TypeMismatch`, or `OutOfRange`. Check signed and unsigned integer bounds, including the explicitly supplied `ISize`/`USize` width. Resolve interned float spelling through the read-only interner and parse/round directly to `F32` or `F64` using roundTiesToEven; a failed parse or non-finite rounded value returns `OutOfRange`. Keep type-path and expected-type resolution, target-width selection, canonical `Str` and unit handling, and workspace-snapshot diagnostic construction in the driver. Reuse this kernel from the existing direct-literal checks without changing the broader inference design.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.3.1–6.3.3 and spec/02 §§2.6.1–2.6.3 define literal kinds, exact integer ranges, and IEEE 754 target-width rounding. Spec/05 §§5.16.2–5.16.5 separately define literal inference variables, defaulting, and the point at which their ranges are checked. Isolating the already-known primitive/type leaf operation in `sai_ty` removes duplicate semantic rules while leaving expected-type resolution, diagnostics with source context, and inference sequencing with their current owners. This is a Stage 0 primitive-literal foundation, not a general body type checker.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_ty typeck::literal::tests --locked` passed all five kernel tests. The driver function-body regression group passed 10 tests, the constant literal group passed 16, `cargo test -p sai_cli --test check_empty_source --locked` passed all 63 tests, and `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` passed all workspace suites. The kernel tests cover signed minimum and one-past-minimum for every fixed width, unsigned limits and negative zero, 32/64-bit pointer widths, direct F32/F64 rounding, underflow and overflow, and malformed/unresolved float symbols. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. Two hostile reviewers found no actionable P0–P2 issues after resolving their boundary-coverage findings. GitHub Actions run #80 (39355569692) passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows for the preceding IR-749 commit; GitHub Actions run #81 (39356752411) passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows after the IR-750 push.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Verify the pure kernel has no dependencies on HIR ownership, source snapshots, or diagnostic emission; accepts only exact scalar literal/type pairs; rejects integer/float and Bool/Char/Byte kind mismatches; uses the caller-supplied 32- or 64-bit width for `ISize`/`USize`; handles signed minimum and unsigned negative-zero boundaries; parses directly to `F32`/`F64`, rounds ties to even without double rounding, accepts nonzero underflow to zero, and rejects parse failures or rounded infinity as out-of-range. Confirm the driver still owns expected-type resolution, target selection, `Str`/unit handling, source-spanned diagnostics, and that no inference/defaulting or general `typeck(owner)` behavior is claimed.

### IR-751: check one annotated local binding in a function body

- **Decision:** Add a bounded compositional Stage 0 body-checking slice for a non-generic, safe, synchronous function with no parameters and a body containing exactly one immutable single-name `let name: T = literal` followed by a plain ASCII tail path resolving by `BindingId` to that local. Require the binding and tail-path spellings to be plain ASCII identifiers, in addition to requiring the binding name not to trigger the current naming-convention gate. A single explicitly typed binding and identity-resolved read establish statement and local-expression checking without taking on inference, general coercions, arbitrary patterns, or another specialized condition spelling. Checking the source spelling as well as the resolved binding prevents raw identifiers from bypassing the unavailable `UNNECESSARY_RAW_IDENT` lint.

The regressions cover valid annotated local reads, initializer mismatch and range errors, return mismatch, exact spans, and gates for unannotated, `var`/`let var`, camel-case and raw names, let-else, destructuring, multiple statements, unknown annotations, computed or nested initializers/tails, unresolved tails, byte strings, aliases, parameters and generics. Hostile review caught both a binding-name lint bypass and a raw tail-reference spelling that resolved to the same `BindingId`; both are gated and covered by regressions, and the follow-up review found no remaining P0–P2 issues. CI for IR-751 will run after push.

### IR-753: copy earlier primitive locals in annotated initializers

### IR-754: constrain one unannotated primitive local from the function result

- **Decision:** Extend the zero-parameter primitive-local body slice to accept exactly one immutable, single-name, unannotated `let value = literal` with a direct Bool, Byte, Char, integer, or floating-point literal initializer, followed by a plain ASCII tail path resolving by `BindingId` to that binding. Integer `ι` and float `φ` variables are constrained by the tail expectation only when the result is in the same literal family; then the primitive literal kernel checks exact range and target-width rounding at the initializer. A family mismatch is reported at the tail. If it leaves a numeric literal variable unresolved, apply the spec's `I64`/`F64` end-of-body default and report any resulting range error at the initializer. Bool, Byte, and Char retain their concrete types and mismatch at the tail unless exactly equal to the return type. Do not add numeric conversions. Keep multiple or mutable locals, computed and non-scalar initializers, destructuring, a different or nonlocal tail binding, aliases, parameters, generics, raw/non-ASCII spellings, and every other unsupported body form gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/05 §§5.16.2–5.16.5 define distinct general, integer-literal, and float-literal variables and require unresolved numeric variables to default to `I64`/`F64` at body end. Spec/06 §§6.3.1–6.3.3 restrict the literal families and define exact range/rounding behavior; §§6.11.1 and 6.12.1 require statement-before-tail checking and make a local visible after its initializer. The tail's explicit result expectation can constrain only an integer or float literal variable of a compatible family. Keeping this to one binding and a direct literal exercises that flow without claiming general inference, arbitrary expression typing, or complete `TypeckResults`. We deliberately preserve the existing source-span diagnostic behavior: family mismatch is anchored on the tail read, while literal range is anchored on the initializer; CLI presentation remains source-position ordered.

After implementation, the driver function-body group passed all 14 tests; all 67 `check_empty_source` CLI tests and the workspace suite passed; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. Declare the `sai:process` dependency with its canonical source URL and `^0.1` range and grant the `wasi:cli` capability to each command; also grant `alloc` to programs that read arguments or use f-strings. Keep the normative source rather than inventing a replacement repository or partial local stub. Document the host convention used by the CLI examples (`argv[0]` contains the program name), the in-memory nature of the task board, and the compiler stages still required.
- **Reason:** A project named Hello World should show text reaching standard output. Spec/16 §16.16.3 defines the standard stream API and includes a greeting command example; spec/08 maps `stdio.write` and `env.read` to `wasi:cli`, while package/01 §§1.10.3 and 1.11.1 require an explicit dependency source and capability policy. The additional projects show a progression from fixed output to input/formatting and then to module boundaries and structured data.
- **Verification:** Ran `sai check` for all three projects with `--target wasm32-wasi`. The current toolchain reports the documented Stage 0/3 dependency feature gates because it does not yet resolve the `sai:process` source dependency. After correcting the task record declaration and construction to the syntax of spec/05 §5.6.1 and spec/06 §6.18.1, the multi-module project reports only those expected stage gates plus the unsupported `@derive` stage; no syntax diagnostics remain. Hostile review verified the package sources, capability policies, project/module layout, and documented CLI assumptions. A public GitHub lookup of the canonical process URL returned 404 on 2026-10-21; package/04 §4.4.3 specifies that standard-package content is supplied by a bundled index. No safe substitute exists in this repository, so the samples do not claim that the dependency resolves today.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Before claiming the samples resolve, confirm that a published `sai:process` source or bundled index entry provides the canonical URL, `^0.1` line, tag, commit, and checksum. Confirm the `wasi:cli`/`alloc` policy for the commands and the documented `argv[0]` assumption. Confirm that Hello World directly emits the greeting and that larger examples are clearly described as in-memory sample code rather than persistent task management.
- **Remaining scope:** Publish the canonical `sai:process` source or bundle its package index entry; then build and execute these samples when dependency resolution, WIT package loading, standard process APIs, component lowering, and the language features used by the larger examples are implemented.

### IR-757: preserve numeric literal inference through flat local sequences

- **Decision:** Generalize the current primitive-local checks to any non-empty source-ordered sequence of immutable, single-name locals. Initializers are restricted to direct scalar primitive literals or plain paths to preceding locals; annotations, when present, must name a supported primitive. A direct unannotated integer or float literal gets its own inference-variable identity, which every plain local copy shares. Compatible annotations and a compatible function result constrain that variable; an incompatible annotated use reports at its initializer, keeps the source variable unresolved for defaulting, and still recovers the destination's declared type. The tail can read any preceding local. Default unresolved numeric variables after checking the tail, in creation order, and report range errors once at each literal's original span. Preserve all current owner, safe-block, spelling, and naming gates; do not add numeric conversions.
- **Reason:** Spec/05 §§5.3.1–5.3.2 and 5.16.2–5.16.5 define primitive local copy behavior, distinct integer/float literal variables, compatible-family constraints, and body-end defaulting. Spec/06 §§6.1.3, 6.3.1–6.3.3, 6.4.1, 6.11.1, and 6.12.1 require literal-family rules, exact local-path typing outside coercion sites, source-ordered statements, coercion at annotated initializers and the tail, and binding visibility only after its initializer. Reusing the same literal-variable identity through a plain local path lets the bounded slice model those rules without claiming general unification or full `typeck(owner)`.
- **Verification:** Added CLI coverage for three-or-more-copy chains, tails reading earlier locals, distinct literal variables, defaulting and source spans, same-family annotation constraints, incompatible annotation recovery, and unsupported self/forward/computed/mutable/destructured/raw/qualified/generic forms. The focused `check_empty_source` suite passed all 77 tests, and `cargo test --workspace --locked` passed after the review regressions were added. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. Hostile review identified two P3 coverage gaps: the chain's prior in-range value did not prove propagation of an out-of-range I8 constraint, and incompatible annotation recovery lacked coverage. Both regressions were added; follow-up hostile review found no actionable findings.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm each literal has independent inference state, plain-path copies preserve the same integer/float variable and original origin, and compatible annotation/tail constraints range-check it exactly once. Confirm incompatible annotations diagnose at their initializer while preserving the source literal for I64/F64 defaulting and binding the destination to its annotation; confirm an incompatible return-family diagnostic remains on the tail. Confirm annotated concrete sources require exact type equality, Bool/Byte/Char stay concrete, target pointer width is used, and no numeric conversions occur. Verify source-order visibility, any-earlier-local tail selection, and all existing owner/name/safe-block gates, with unsupported forms still gated. This remains a bounded type-checking slice rather than general local inference or complete `TypeckResults`.
- **Remaining scope:** General inference and constraint solving; arbitrary initializer/tail expressions; nested blocks, patterns, mutable bindings, parameters, and control flow; general diagnostic recovery; complete `TypeckResults`; and full Stage 0 body checking remain incomplete.

### IR-758: copy a concrete primitive parameter into flat locals

- **Decision:** Extend the flat-local checker to accept exactly one named, immutable, non-`self` parameter whose type resolves to a supported primitive. Require the HIR body parameter to match the signature name and resolve to a `BindingId` classified as `Param`; seed only that binding into the initial type environment with its concrete type. Local initializers may copy it by a plain path or copy earlier locals. An annotated copy requires exact type identity; an unannotated copy inherits the same concrete type. Keep the tail bound to a local declared in the block, not the parameter itself, and add no numeric conversions. Preserve the existing public, safe, synchronous, nongeneric, name and body gates.
- **Reason:** Spec/05 §§5.3.1–5.3.2 and 5.16.2–5.16.5 establish concrete parameter types and primitive copy behavior. Spec/06 §§6.1.3, 6.2.2, 6.4.1, 6.11.1, and 6.12.1 require exact local-path typing outside coercion sites, source-order initializer checking, and the parameter/local binding identities used by resolution. An annotated local initializer is a coercion site, but two already-concrete primitive types do not widen implicitly, so this slice checks exact equality.
- **Verification:** Added CLI coverage for annotated and unannotated parameter copies, exact I32-to-F32 mismatch at the initializer, return mismatch at the local tail, and gates for multiple/mutable/self parameters and a parameter used as the tail. The focused `check_empty_source` suite passed all 80 tests after the parameter-tail regression was added, and the existing 16 driver body-check tests passed. `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Hostile review found one P3 gap: the parameter-tail gate lacked a regression. After adding it, follow-up review confirmed the test directly exercises the local-only tail requirement and found no P0–P2 issues.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm exactly one named immutable non-`self` supported primitive parameter seeds the initial environment by its resolved `BindingId`, and only preceding local bindings are introduced later. Confirm the same-name body parameter is a `Param`; a path to the parameter can be used as a local initializer, while the tail must resolve to a block local. Verify annotated copies require exact type equality, unannotated copies preserve the parameter type, mismatches have initializer/tail primary spans, and no numeric conversion is applied. Confirm multi-parameter, mutable, `self`, user-defined alias, parameter-tail, and other previously gated forms remain gated.
- **Remaining scope:** More than one parameter, parameter inference and general body environments, arbitrary local expressions, mutable/destructured locals, nested control flow, general coercion and type-variable solving, complete `TypeckResults`, and full Stage 0 body checking remain incomplete.

### IR-759: use multiple primitive parameters as flat-local sources

- **Decision:** Extend the parameter-source local form to any number of parameters when every signature/body pair has the same lint-clean name, is immutable and non-`self`, resolves to a `Param` binding, and has a directly supported primitive type. Seed all parameter bindings into the initial local type environment. Let initializers may copy any parameter or preceding local, and the tail remains restricted to a local declared in the block. Annotated copies require exact primitive equality; unannotated copies inherit the concrete source type. If any parameter fails these requirements, preserve the feature gate.
- **Reason:** Spec/05 §§5.3.1–5.3.2 and 5.16.2–5.16.5 define parameter and local value types. Spec/06 §§6.1.3, 6.2.2, 6.4.1, 6.11.1, and 6.12.1 establish path type lookup, resolved binding identity, exact local-copy semantics, and source-ordered local visibility. The existing initial environment is already keyed by `BindingId`, so seeding the eligible parameters extends that model without changing inference or coercion semantics.
- **Verification:** Added CLI tests for annotated and unannotated copies from two distinct parameters, a three-parameter copy using the third binding, a type mismatch at an initializer with its primary span, and gates for mutable and unsupported (`Str`) parameters. The focused `check_empty_source` suite passed all 83 tests, the 16 driver function-body tests passed, `cargo test --workspace --locked` passed, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` plus `git diff --check` passed. Hostile review requested the three-parameter regression, which was added; follow-up review confirmed it covers the third binding and found no remaining actionable issues.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm all signature/body parameter pairs are checked in order and tied by name plus `BindingId`, and every eligible binding starts concrete in the initial environment before any local initializer. Confirm all parameters must be named, immutable, non-`self`, and supported primitive types; one ineligible parameter gates the form. Confirm paths to any parameter or earlier local may initialize a local, but only a block local may be the tail. Verify exact-type annotation checks and source spans, continued support for existing zero/one-parameter body slices and conditional forms, and gates for mutable, self, unsupported, and user-defined-alias parameter types.
- **Remaining scope:** Arbitrary parameter and local types; parameter inference; expression initializers and computed tails; mutable/destructured locals; nested blocks/control flow; general coercion and type-variable solving; complete `TypeckResults`; and full Stage 0 body checking remain incomplete.

### IR-760: allow a visible parameter as the tail after locals

- **Decision:** After the flat-local checker validates one or more source-ordered immutable local statements, allow its plain tail path to resolve to any binding in the environment accumulated so far, including an eligible function parameter in the initial environment. Resolve by `BindingId`; constrain/check the selected concrete type against the explicit result and report mismatch at the tail. Preserve self/forward and other existing body gates, and add no numeric conversions.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.1.3, 6.4.1, and 6.11.1 make the tail a value expression checked against its enclosing result and assign local-path types from resolved bindings; §6.12.1 makes each local visible after its initializer. A parameter is already visible throughout the body, and the existing direct-parameter tail slice already checks it. Permitting that binding after supported local statements applies the same semantics without expanding the set of accepted initializers or local types.
- **Verification:** Added CLI coverage for a parameter returned after a concrete local copy, a later parameter returned after a local, a return-type mismatch whose primary span is the parameter tail, and shadowing where the initializer resolves to the parameter while the tail resolves to the local. The focused `check_empty_source` suite passed all 84 tests; `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Hostile review found P3 gaps around parameter shadowing and multi-parameter tails; regressions now cover both. Follow-up hostile review confirmed the gaps are closed and found no remaining actionable issues.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm the tail must resolve by `BindingId` to any parameter seeded in the initial environment or a local introduced by the validated sequence; self/forward or other unseen bindings remain gated. Confirm a local shadowing a parameter selects its own binding identity, exact primitive result equality is preserved, mismatches point to the tail, and the behavior without local statements remains unchanged.
- **Remaining scope:** Computed tails, non-primitive parameter/local types, parameter inference, mutable/destructured locals, nested blocks/control flow, general coercion and type-variable solving, complete `TypeckResults`, and full Stage 0 body checking remain incomplete.

### IR-761: primitive comparisons in flat-local initializers

- **Decision:** Extend the source-ordered flat-local checker to accept one direct comparison initializer (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=`) with two plain paths to eligible parameters or preceding locals. Resolve both paths by `BindingId` and require their already-concrete types to be the same supported primitive. The result is `Bool`; an optional annotation must be `Bool`. On a primitive type mismatch, diagnose at the right operand path and recover the expression as `Bool`. On a non-`Bool` annotation, diagnose at the initializer and still give the local its actual `Bool` result type. Keep literal operands, arithmetic and logical expressions, nesting, conversions, aliases, nonlocal or qualified paths, and unresolved numeric literal operands gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.8.7, 6.11.1, and 6.12.1 require same-type comparison operands, a `Bool` result, source-ordered statements, and binding visibility only after an initializer. All six comparison operators are defined for the supported primitive set, so the bounded kernel can reuse resolved primitive local types and preserve binding identity without introducing user-trait solving, expression inference, or numeric conversions. Reporting the right path makes the mismatching operand explicit. Recovering as `Bool` preserves the actual expression result for later local reads and tail checking even when the annotation is invalid.
- **Verification:** Both focused `sai_ty::typeck::body` kernel tests pass, covering all six operators for every supported concrete primitive, mismatched types, non-comparison operators, and an unsupported type. The focused CLI filter passes all seven comparison tests, covering each operator, parameter and preceding-local operands, Bool annotations, a right-operand mismatch span, non-Bool annotation recovery through the tail, shadowing, source order, and gated shapes including an unresolved numeric literal local. Hostile review found that the unresolved-literal gate lacked an explicit regression; the test was added, and follow-up review found no remaining actionable issues. `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm each operand is a plain, single-segment path resolving to a seeded parameter or a preceding local, and that shadowing chooses the binding resolved at that source location. Confirm all six operators accept same-typed supported primitives, mismatched types are diagnosed on the right operand, and invalid annotations report at the comparison initializer while recovery remains `Bool` through the tail. Confirm unresolved literal variables do not gain comparison-driven inference and literal, arithmetic, logical, nested, nonlocal/qualified, aliased, conversion, self/forward, mutable/destructured, and unsupported-type forms remain gated.
- **Remaining scope:** Comparison inference for unresolved literal locals; literal operands; arithmetic/logical/nested expressions; general local expression typing; custom types and operator trait selection; coercions and numeric conversions; general patterns, control flow, and complete `TypeckResults` remain incomplete.

### IR-762: logical operators in flat-local initializers

- **Decision:** Extend the flat-local checker to accept one direct top-level `and` or `or` initializer with two plain paths to eligible parameters or preceding locals. Resolve both operands by `BindingId`, check each against `Bool` in written order, and report each non-`Bool` supported primitive path at that operand. The expression result recovers to `Bool`; a non-`Bool` annotation reports at the initializer and the local still has type `Bool`. Preserve the original operator and expression tree.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.8.8, 6.11.1, 6.12.1, and 6.23 require `Bool` operands, a `Bool` result, source-ordered local visibility, and conditional right-operand evaluation for `and` and `or`. Checking both operand types in source order adds no runtime transformation, so short-circuit behavior is unchanged. `BindingId` preserves correct lookup when locals shadow parameters or earlier locals. The narrow path-only form avoids introducing nested expression checking or inference.
- **Verification:** The focused `sai_ty::typeck::body` kernel test covers `Bool`, every other supported primitive mismatch, and an unsupported type. All four focused CLI tests pass, covering parameter/local/mixed/repeated paths, both operators, shadowing, source-order diagnostics and operand spans, non-`Bool` annotation recovery, and gates for nested, negated, literal, arithmetic, comparison, qualified, nonlocal, unresolved, self-referential, and forward-reference forms. `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Hostile review found a missing CLI regression for an unresolved numeric-literal local used as a logical operand; the implementation already gated this case, and the focused regression now passes. Follow-up hostile review confirmed the regression closes the gap and found no remaining actionable issues.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm both `and` and `or` accept only two plain paths resolved to eligible parameter or preceding-local bindings, including repeated and shadowed bindings. Confirm every non-`Bool` operand gets one mismatch on its own path in written order and recovery remains `Bool` through the annotation, later locals, and tail. Confirm the implementation preserves the operator and short-circuit behavior, while nested/chained, `not`, literal, arithmetic, comparison, qualified/nonlocal, alias, unresolved/self/forward, and unsupported forms remain gated.

### IR-763: unary `not` in flat-local initializers

- **Decision:** Extend the source-ordered flat-local checker to accept one unary `not` whose operand is a plain path resolving by `BindingId` to an eligible parameter or preceding local. Require `Bool`; diagnose a non-`Bool` supported primitive at the operand path and recover the initializer result as `Bool`. Permit omitted or `Bool` annotations; diagnose a different supported primitive annotation at the initializer and retain `Bool` for later bindings and the tail. Keep nested/double negation, `not` over comparisons/logical expressions/literals/computed expressions, nonlocal or qualified paths, user-defined aliases, and unresolved/self/forward paths gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.6 defines `not` only for `Bool`, §6.8.8 gives its `Bool` result, and §§6.4.1, 6.11.1, and 6.12.1 require local path types, expression-result recovery, and source-ordered binding visibility. Resolving the single path by `BindingId` reuses the existing concrete local environment and preserves shadowing without opening general unary-expression or local-inference checking.
- **Verification:** The focused kernel test `logical_and_not_operands_require_bool_and_reject_unsupported_types` passes. All four CLI tests matching `primitive_local_not` pass: parameter/local use and shadowing, non-`Bool` operand span plus `Bool` recovery, source-ordered operand/annotation diagnostics with spans and recovery through the tail, and gates for nested/double `not`, comparisons, logical/computed/literal expressions, unresolved numeric-literal locals, aliases, qualified/nonlocal paths, and self/forward references. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` passes all workspace test suites (3,254 tests); `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm exactly one unary `not` over a plain path resolving to an eligible parameter or preceding local is accepted; all other unary/nested/computed forms remain gated. Confirm non-`Bool` operand diagnostics point to the path, annotation diagnostics point to the initializer, both error paths recover to `Bool` for later locals and tail checking, shadowed names use the resolved `BindingId`, and initializer diagnostics retain source order.

### IR-764: compare a flat-local path with a scalar literal

- **Decision:** Extend flat-local comparison initializers to one direct comparison with exactly one plain path to an eligible parameter or preceding local and one direct scalar `Bool`, `Char`, `Byte`, integer, or float literal, in either order. Resolve the path by `BindingId`; retain all six built-in comparison operators and the `Bool` result/annotation recovery. Check a right-side literal against the path type. For a literal on the left, follow the existing conditional check's literal families: integers may unify with any integer primitive, floats with `F32` or `F64`, and fixed `Bool`, `Char`, and `Byte` literals require their exact primitive type. Report left-literal family mismatches at the path using the literal's inferred/default (`I64`/`F64`) or fixed type, and report literal type/range errors at the literal. Preserve the selected target's pointer width. Keep repeated/shadowed binding identity intact. Gate literal/literal, string/unit, computed or nested expressions, arithmetic/logical expressions, nonlocal/qualified/custom-alias paths, unresolved numeric-local sources, and self/forward references.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.3.1–6.3.3 define literal families and range checking; §6.8.7 checks the right comparison operand against the left operand's type and gives the comparison a `Bool` result; §§6.4.1, 6.11.1, and 6.12.1 establish binding identity, source-ordered visibility, and initializer result checking. The literal-left family rule mirrors the established one-parameter conditional comparison behavior, so literal inference direction and mismatch spans stay consistent across supported body slices. A single direct path/literal pair reuses primitive literal checking and target-width range logic without adding expression inference or general operator resolution.
- **Verification:** The focused `sai_ty::typeck::body` literal-family test passes, and all nine focused CLI comparison tests pass. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` passes all workspace suites (3,260 tests); `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass. Regressions cover both operand orders and all six comparison operators; all five scalar literal classes; parameters, preceding locals, shadowing, and transparent `Int`/`UInt`; type/family/range mismatches with exact spans (including an out-of-range left literal that also mismatches the path family); annotation and `Bool` recovery; source-span diagnostic order; 32-bit versus 64-bit `USize` range behavior; and unsupported shapes. Hostile review found that a left numeric literal with a family mismatch skipped default-type range checking; the checker now emits that independent literal diagnostic, and the focused regression passes.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Verify both orders accept only one direct scalar literal and a plain path that resolves by `BindingId` to an eligible parameter or preceding local. Confirm right-side literals check against the path type, left-side literals use the documented numeric/fixed families and mismatch location, target-width range errors point to the literal, all operand errors and bad annotations recover to `Bool`, shadowing and diagnostic source order are preserved, and the literal/operator expression is not rewritten. Confirm literal/literal, string/unit, computed/nested, logical/arithmetic, unresolved numeric local, qualified/nonlocal, custom alias, self/forward, and unsupported forms remain gated.
- **Remaining scope:** General expression inference and nested operators; const and nonlocal path operands; user-defined aliases and comparison traits; strings and unit; coercions and numeric conversions; mutable/destructured locals; control flow; and complete `TypeckResults` remain incomplete.

### IR-765: add two flat-local numeric paths

- **Decision:** Extend flat-local initializers to accept one direct `+` between plain, one-segment, non-generic paths resolving by `BindingId` to eligible parameters or preceding locals. Require matching concrete primitive integer types or matching `F32`/`F64`; do not widen. A right operand with another supported numeric type reports `TYPE_MISMATCH` at that path and recovers with the left type. An omitted or matching annotation is accepted. A different supported primitive annotation reports on the whole initializer and the local recovers to the declared annotation. Preserve the original addition expression. Keep numeric literals, unresolved numeric locals, nonnumeric primitives, user-defined aliases, nonlocal/qualified paths, nested/computed expressions, other operators, mutable/destructured bindings, and self/forward references gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.2 synthesizes the left operand and checks the right against it, which anchors an operand mismatch on the right; §6.8.3 defines exact addition only for integer primitives and `F32`/`F64`, with no widening. §§6.11.1 and 6.12.1 require source-ordered statements and make each binding visible after its initializer. The annotation is the local's declared type under `(T-Let-Ann)`, so when its coercion-site check fails, retaining that declared type lets later statements and the tail continue with a stable recovery type. Constraining this slice to a direct path pair avoids introducing general expression inference, arithmetic lowering, overflow evaluation, or user-defined operator resolution.
- **Verification:** The focused kernel arithmetic-type test and five focused CLI addition tests pass. They cover matching integer/float operands, annotated and inferred locals, parameters and preceding locals, shadowed binding identity, right-path mismatch and left-type recovery, annotation-span mismatch and annotation-type recovery, source-ordered diagnostics, and gated literal, unresolved, nested/computed, non-add, nonnumeric, alias, nonlocal/qualified, self/forward, mutable, and destructured forms. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Hostile snapshot review found no actionable P1–P3 findings.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm that only one direct addition over paths to eligible parameter or preceding-local bindings is accepted, and that types must be identical primitive integers or identical `F32`/`F64` with no widening. Verify that a right mismatch is anchored on the right path and recovers as the left type; a bad annotation is anchored on the initializer and subsequent reads use the annotation type. Confirm binding identity handles shadowing and statement order, and that literals, unresolved numeric locals, custom aliases, nonlocal/qualified paths, nested/computed expressions, other operators, Byte/Char/Bool, mutable/destructured bindings, self/forward references, and other unsupported forms remain gated.
- **Remaining scope:** Subtraction and other operators; literal operands and unresolved numeric arithmetic inference; nested or computed expressions; user-defined operator traits; custom aliases; coercions and numeric conversions; mutable/destructured locals; general control flow; arithmetic evaluation and overflow checking; and complete `TypeckResults` remain incomplete.

### IR-766: add subtraction and multiplication to flat-local arithmetic

- **Decision:** Extend the direct two-path arithmetic initializer from `+` to `-` and `*`. Each operand must resolve by `BindingId` to an eligible parameter or preceding local, and both must have the same concrete primitive integer type or the same `F32`/`F64`; do not widen. The expression result is its operand type. Preserve IR-765's right-path mismatch diagnostic and left-type recovery, plus whole-initializer annotation diagnostics and recovery to the declared type. Preserve the original HIR operator. Keep literal/unresolved-literal operands, other operators, `Byte`/`Char`/`Bool`, aliases, nonlocal or qualified paths, nested/computed forms, mutable/destructured locals, and self/forward references gated. Sharing IR-765's narrow primitive arithmetic kernel applies those rules without general expression inference, operator traits, or runtime behavior.

Hostile review found no actionable P1–P3 findings.

Confirm right mismatches report on the right path and recover to the left type, while bad annotations report on the whole initializer and recover to the declared type. Confirm binding identity handles shadowing and statement order, and all listed literal, other-operator, nonnumeric, alias, nonlocal, qualified, nested/computed, mutable/destructured, and self/forward forms remain gated. ### IR-767: add a numeric literal to a flat-local addition

- **Decision:** Extend only the direct `path + literal` form: the left side must be a concrete primitive integer, `F32`, or `F64` path to an eligible parameter or preceding local, and the right side must be one direct integer or floating-point literal. Check the literal against the left path type, retain the left type after operand errors, and preserve annotation mismatch recovery to the declared type. At this step, keep `literal + path`, unresolved numeric locals, fixed-kind literals, nonnumeric path types, and computed or nested shapes gated; right-literal `-` and `*` were deferred to and are implemented by IR-768.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.2 synthesizes the left operand and checks the right against it. This lets the narrow addition slice reuse the existing primitive literal checker for exact family diagnostics, range checks, and target pointer width without introducing fresh literal variables or changing their defaulting. The direct right-literal form was implemented first, leaving literal-left arithmetic for a later slice. That is an implementation boundary, not a language restriction: spec/06 §6.8.2 synthesizes the left operand to `ι` or `φ` and then checks the right path against that variable, so the right path can constrain it under spec/05 §5.16. Implementing the form requires this bounded checker to carry a literal variable through right-path checking and define recovery after a family mismatch. Integer literals checked against a float type remain a §3.7.6 type mismatch; no implicit integer-to-float conversion is added. The expression result remains the left type after a right-literal error, while the local annotation still owns recovery after a whole-initializer mismatch.
- **Verification:** The focused body kernel suite passes (6 tests). Eight focused CLI addition tests pass, covering all integer/floating literal shapes, fixed-literal gates, left-literal and computed-shape gates, annotation recovery, and exact operand spans. The target-width cases accept signed/unsigned 32-bit and 64-bit boundaries and diagnose out-of-range `ISize`/`USize` literals at the literal on wasm32. Existing flat-local subtraction/multiplication (4 CLI tests) and comparison (8 CLI tests) regressions pass. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing gate tests now use unresolved-literal or `-` forms where a concrete path-plus-literal case is no longer outside the slice. Hostile review found no actionable P0–P3 findings.

Confirm annotation mismatches use the whole initializer span and recover to the annotation. Confirm literal-left forms remain gated at this staged implementation step (spec/06 §6.8.2 permits the right path to constrain the synthesized `ι`/`φ` literal; IR-770 is the planned follow-up), while fixed literals, nonnumeric paths, unresolved numeric locals, nested/computed expressions, and every other unsupported shape remain gated. ### IR-768: add right numeric literals to subtraction and multiplication

- **Decision:** Extend only the direct `path - literal` and `path * literal` local-initializer forms. The left side must resolve by `BindingId` to a concrete primitive integer, `F32`, or `F64` parameter or preceding local; the right side must be one direct integer or floating-point literal. Check the literal against the path type with the existing primitive-literal checker, report literal-kind and range errors at the literal expression, and recover the expression to the left type. Accept omitted or matching annotations; on a different supported annotation, report over the initializer and recover the local to its declared type. An unparenthesized integer or floating-point token directly preceded by unary `-` remains a direct literal because HIR folds it into a single `Lit::Int { negated: true }` or `Lit::Float { negated: true }` node. Thus `-128` fits `I8`, `-129` is out of range, and an unsigned integer accepts a negated literal only when its value is zero (`-0` fits `U8`; `-1` is out of range). The literal span includes its directly folded sign. Defer literal-left arithmetic to IR-770; spec/06 §6.8.2 permits the right path to constrain a left `ι`/`φ` literal variable, but this slice does not implement that flow. Also defer `/`, `%`, wrapping operators, custom aliases, arithmetic evaluation, and overflow checking.
- **Reason:** Spec/02 §2.6.1 and spec/06 §§6.3.1 and 6.8.2–6.8.3 define a directly negated integer token as one negative constant and require its range to be checked against the expected integer type. HIR already folds a direct unary minus over integer and float tokens into signed literal values while preserving the complete expression span. Reusing the existing literal checker therefore provides the specified signed boundary, unsigned `-0` rule, float-width parsing, target `ISize`/`USize` bounds, and literal-local diagnostics without adding general inference. Spec/06 §6.8.2 directs the right operand from the synthesized left type; this bounded form preserves that direction and the existing recovery contract.
- **Verification:** Focused kernel tests passed 2/2; the initial IR-768 CLI set passed 7/7 before explicit negative-boundary assertions were added. The current `primitive_sub_mul_local` CLI filter passed 5/5 after those assertions were added, including `-128`, `-129`, `-0`, `-1`, and negative float literals. Existing IR-767 addition regressions passed 8/8. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` passed all 3,286 tests on the rebased branch, including the corrected gate regressions. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. These are type-checking tests; they do not establish runtime arithmetic evaluation or overflow behavior.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Verify that only one direct numeric literal is accepted to the right of a concrete eligible path for `-` or `*`, including a directly folded negative integer; check `-128`/`-129` against `I8`, `-0`/`-1` against `U8`, and ensure the primary span includes the sign. Check that negative float literals are direct HIR literals and follow the existing F32/F64 range rules. Confirm family mismatches and range errors point to the literal, selected target pointer width is honored, operator errors recover to the left type, and annotation mismatch recovers to the annotation. Confirm literal-left forms, unresolved numeric-local inference, `/`, `%`, wrapping operators, nested/computed expressions, custom aliases, evaluation, and overflow checking remain outside this slice.
- **Remaining scope:** Literal-left flat-local arithmetic was deferred at the IR-768 step and is implemented by IR-770. Unresolved numeric-local arithmetic inference; `/`, `%`, wrapping and user-defined operators; nested/computed expressions; custom aliases and coercions; mutable/destructured locals; general control flow and complete `TypeckResults`; arithmetic evaluation and overflow diagnostics remain unimplemented.

### IR-770: infer literal-left flat-local arithmetic

- **Decision:** Support one direct integer or floating-point literal on the left of `+`, `-`, or `*`, with one eligible concrete numeric parameter or preceding-local path on the right. For a matching literal family, constrain the left `ι`/`φ` variable to the right path type, range-check the literal at its own span (including a directly folded negative sign and selected pointer width), and give the expression the right path type. For a family mismatch, report `TYPE_MISMATCH` at the right path using the literal family's default type (`I64` or `F64`), leave the left literal variable unresolved, and retain that variable as the expression/local result. Let a later annotation or tail constrain it; otherwise default and range-check it at body end. Keep unresolved numeric-local arithmetic, fixed-kind literals, other operators, nested/computed expressions, aliases, arithmetic evaluation, and overflow checking gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.2 synthesizes an integer or float literal to `ι`/`φ` and checks the right operand against that variable; spec/05 §5.16.2 permits unification only with the matching integer or float family. The existing body checker already preserves literal variables across local copies, applies later annotations and tail expectations, and checks unresolved values against `I64`/`F64` at body end. Reusing that path follows the specified inference direction, preserves later context after an operand mismatch, and avoids introducing general arithmetic inference. The cross-family recovery makes the visible mismatch deterministic at the constraining path while keeping the failed literal variable available for the checker's existing constraint/defaulting behavior.
- **Verification:** The arithmetic-kernel inference matrix passes for `+`, `-`, and `*` across all integer primitives and `F32`/`F64`. Six focused `primitive_arithmetic` CLI regressions pass for parameter/local binding, all operators and primitive families, family-mismatch diagnostics, later annotation and tail constraints, body-end defaulting, negative-literal spans, and wasm32/wasm64 pointer-width bounds. Five existing `primitive_sub_mul_local` regressions and eight `unsupported_primitive` gate regressions pass. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` passes all 3,293 tests. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass. These checks establish type-checking behavior only; they do not establish arithmetic execution or overflow behavior.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Verify all three operators with integer and float literals against same-family concrete paths, including binding identity, direct negative literals, exact literal/path spans, and wasm32/wasm64 pointer-width range checks. Confirm family mismatches report at the right path with the documented default-type expectation and do not prematurely resolve the left literal variable; matching later annotation/tail constraints must still apply, while an unconstrained variable defaults and range-checks at its origin. Confirm annotation mismatch recovery, source-ordered diagnostics, fixed literals, unresolved numeric paths, computed/nested operands, other operators, and arithmetic execution/overflow remain outside this slice. Hostile review requested explicit tail-constraint and sign-inclusive negative-range regressions; both were added and the follow-up review found no remaining actionable findings.
- **Remaining scope:** General expression inference, unresolved numeric-local arithmetic, `/`, `%`, wrapping and overloaded operators, custom aliases and coercions, nested/computed expressions, arithmetic evaluation and overflow checking, and complete `TypeckResults`.

### IR-771: type-check flat-local division

- **Decision:** Extend the bounded immutable single-name local arithmetic initializer to direct `/` between two eligible concrete numeric paths, one path and one direct numeric literal on the right, or one direct numeric literal and path on the left. Resolve paths by `BindingId`; require exact type equality for two concrete operands; and reuse the existing literal-family inference, range checking, diagnostic spans, and annotation recovery for either literal order. Support the ten integer types and `F32`/`F64` with no widening or conversion. Type checking accepts an integer literal divisor of zero; do not evaluate division or check runtime `DivByZero` or signed `MIN / -1` overflow here. Keep `%`, wrapping operations, literal/literal, nested/computed operands, aliases, and other unsupported shapes gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.8.2–6.8.3 define left-directed operand checking, exact matching numeric operand types, division over integer and float families, and integer runtime panic cases. Spec/05 §5.16 permits the existing `ι`/`φ` literal variables to unify with their matching families. Reusing the established arithmetic path keeps binding identity, literal inference and defaulting, target-width range checks, and error recovery consistent while leaving runtime semantics for the later MIR/backend stage.

### IR-772: type-check flat-local remainder

- **Decision:** Extend the immutable single-name local arithmetic initializer to direct `%` between matching concrete integer paths or between an integer path and one direct integer literal in either order. Resolve paths by `BindingId`, require exact integer type equality for path pairs, and reuse the current numeric-literal inference, target-width checks, diagnostic spans, and annotation recovery. Permit integer `% 0` through type checking. For float-left `%` in these same direct shapes, check the right operand against the float left type before emitting `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED` on the whole expression; add help that recommends the float `rem` method. If a left float literal has not selected F32 or F64 yet, describe the unsupported operator as applying to floating-point values without choosing a width; a right-family mismatch retains the existing F64 default for its type-mismatch diagnostic. Keep literal/literal, unresolved numeric locals, Byte/Bool/Char, aliases, wrapping operators, and nested/computed forms gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.8.2–6.8.3 defines left-directed operand checking, integer remainder, and `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED` for float `%`; spec/16 §16.8.4 names the replacement method `rem`. Separating the remainder check from generic arithmetic prevents float operands from being accepted merely because `/` supports them. Checking the RHS first preserves type mismatch diagnostics and expression recovery before reporting the unsupported float operator. Avoiding a premature width in the operator error lets a later F32 annotation resolve a still-unresolved float literal without making the error claim F64. Runtime `RemByZero`, signed `MIN % -1`, and arithmetic evaluation belong to the later MIR/backend slice.
- **Verification:** `cargo fmt --all`, `git diff --check`, the focused float-remainder diagnostic test, the unsupported-shape gate test, `cargo test -p sai_ty --lib --locked` (49 passed), and `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` all passed. Hostile review confirmed the Byte/Bool/Char right-path gate and unresolved float-literal diagnostic behavior, with no blocking findings.
- **Review:** **Review required:** The implementation intentionally keeps remainder runtime semantics outside this slice. Review the stated future-scope boundary before adding evaluation, especially division-by-zero and signed `MIN % -1` behavior. Confirm the generic float-literal wording remains useful if later type inference gains annotation-directed literal-family checks. Do not infer execution or runtime remainder behavior from these type-checking tests.
- **Remaining scope:** Remainder execution, `RemByZero` and signed `MIN % -1` runtime semantics, wrapping arithmetic, general expression inference, aliases and coercions, nested/computed operands, and complete `TypeckResults`.

### IR-773: type-check flat-local wrapping operators

- **Decision:** Extend the immutable single-name local initializer to direct path/path `+%`, `-%`, and `*%` between the ten integer primitives, requiring the right path to match the left type exactly. Resolve each path by `BindingId`; mismatched right paths report `TYPE_MISMATCH` at the right operand and recover with the left type, while a mismatched supported annotation reports on the whole initializer and recovers to the annotation. Known non-integer scalar paths report `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED` over the expression. When their types differ, primitive numeric, `Byte`, and `Bool` left operands also report the left-directed right-path mismatch; `Char` follows the missing-trait operator error without a synthetic right mismatch. Keep literals, unresolved numeric locals, custom aliases, nested/computed operands, mutable locals, and unsupported owner shapes gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.2 fixes primitive binary operand checking from the left, and §6.8.4 defines wrapping operators only for integer primitives while requiring `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED` elsewhere. Limiting this step to path pairs exercises binding identity, exact type matching, and error recovery without extending literal inference or claiming runtime wrapping behavior. The `Char` distinction follows §6.8.2: unlike numeric, `Byte`, and `Bool` left operands, `Char` falls through to operator-trait selection.
- **Verification:** `cargo fmt --all`, `git diff --check`, the three focused wrapping-operator CLI tests, the unsupported-shape gate test, the focused IR-772 float-remainder regression, `cargo test -p sai_ty --lib --locked` (49 passed), and `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet` all passed. Hostile review found no correctness gaps in operator routing, type recovery, non-integer diagnostics, or unsupported-shape gates.

Confirm this type-checking slice does not claim modulo-2^w runtime behavior from tests of well-typed expressions.
- **Remaining scope:** Wrapping literals, runtime/MIR execution, general expression inference, aliases and coercions, nested/computed operands, and complete `TypeckResults`.

### IR-775: accept left-side integer literals for wrapping operators

- **Decision:** Extend direct `+%`, `-%`, and `*%` local initializers with one integer literal on the left and one eligible primitive path on the right. For integer right paths, constrain the left literal's `ι` to the exact path type and reuse target-specific range checks at the literal span. ### IR-776: type-check flat-local bitwise path pairs

- **Decision:** Accept one direct path/path `&`, `|`, or `^` local initializer when both paths resolve to concrete supported primitive locals or parameters in source order. Matching integer and `Byte` pairs are accepted. For integer/`Byte` left operands, a differing supported primitive right operand gets a right-path `TYPE_MISMATCH` and the expression recovers to the left type. For `Bool`, `F32`, or `F64` left operands, report a mismatch first if the supported right type differs, then report `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`; same-type pairs get only the latter. A `Char` left operand follows rule 3 and reports an unsupported operator trait naming both operand types without a synthetic mismatch. Keep literals, unresolved numeric locals, unary `~`, shifts, aliases, self/forward references, nested/computed shapes, and unsupported owners gated. Preserve logical `and`/`or` and the original expression; do not claim lowering or runtime behavior.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.8.2 and 6.8.5 distinguish left-directed primitive operand checking from rule-3 operator-trait selection, define bitwise operators only for integer primitives and `Byte`, and leave `Bool` without bitwise support. The explicit left-type recovery lets supported local statements and tails continue after a right mismatch, while diagnostics retain the required source order. Direct paths keep binding resolution, expression inference, trait selection, and runtime semantics outside this slice.
- **Verification:** `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo test -p sai_driver function_body_type_check_ --locked` (19 tests), `cargo test -p sai_cli primitive_bitwise_ --locked` (5 tests), and `cargo test --workspace --locked` all pass. The CLI integration fixtures run one public function per package because that is the current `sai check` body-analysis boundary; driver tests cover all ten integer types and every operator. Hostile review found no P0–P2 issues and confirmed operand recovery, diagnostics, spans, gated forms, and the lack of lowering/runtime claims; its P3 unreachable-branch finding was removed. `git diff --check` is included in final review.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm matching integer and `Byte` pairs accept all three operators; integer/`Byte` mismatch recovery uses the left type; `Bool`/float mismatches precede `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, while same-type pairs produce only that operator diagnostic; and `Char` uses rule-3 wording with both types and no synthetic mismatch. Confirm exact source spans and annotation recovery, `and`/`or` preservation, and that literal, unresolved numeric local, `~`, shift, alias, self/forward, nested/computed, and unsupported-owner forms remain gated. Confirm no test or documentation claims bitwise lowering or execution. The current CLI tests deliberately isolate each public function because wider body analysis remains gated for multi-function source candidates.
- **Remaining scope:** Bitwise literals, `~`, shifts, computed/nested expressions, general operator and trait resolution, aliases/coercions, lowering/runtime semantics, and complete `TypeckResults`.

### IR-777: type-check direct right integer literals for flat-local bitwise operators

- **Decision:** Extend the IR-776 `&`, `|`, and `^` form to one eligible integer-typed left path followed by one direct integer literal. Accept all ten integer primitives, checking the literal against the exact path type and recovering the expression to that type after mismatch or range errors. Recognize `Byte` as a supported left operand but report a literal `TYPE_MISMATCH`: the integer literal family does not include `Byte`. For `Bool`, `F32`, and `F64`, the body checker records the left-directed literal mismatch before whole-expression `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`; CLI presentation sorts by source span, so it can print the enclosing operator diagnostic first. Keep `Char` with an integer literal gated until operator-trait inference is implemented. Literal-left, literal/literal, other literal kinds, unresolved locals, aliases, nested/computed operands, `~`, shifts, and unsupported owners remain gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.2 requires checking the right operand against the left operand's type. Reuse of the existing annotated-literal checker preserves signed literal spans and target pointer-width range rules. `Byte` is a distinct primitive and must not be accepted as an integer literal's inferred type. The unsupported `Bool`/float operator diagnostic remains necessary after reporting the literal mismatch, while the expression's recovery type keeps later annotations and uses checkable. Gating `Char` avoids inventing a right-type selection rule before trait inference exists.
- **Verification:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass. `cargo test -p sai_driver function_body_type_check_ --locked` passes all 20 focused driver tests; `cargo test -p sai_cli primitive_bitwise --locked` passes all 15 matching CLI integration tests, including type/operator coverage, boundary and target-pointer-width range checks with exact spans, recovery, and gates; `cargo test --workspace --locked` passes. Hostile review found no P0–P2 issues. Its P3 note about checker error collection order versus CLI span-sorted presentation was clarified in both implementation chapters and this review entry.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm the ten integer primitives accept each of `&`, `|`, and `^` with a direct right integer literal; fixed-width and wasm32/wasm64 pointer-width boundaries use the complete literal span; `Byte` reports only the literal mismatch and recovers to `Byte`; and `Bool`/float body-checker errors record the right-literal mismatch before the whole-expression unsupported operator while CLI output sorts the enclosing expression span first. Confirm later uses and annotation mismatches recover, and that literal-left, literal/literal, non-integer literals, unresolved locals, aliases, self/forward, nested/computed forms, shifts, `~`, and `Char` with an integer literal remain gated. Confirm no lowering or runtime behavior is claimed.
- **Remaining scope:** Literal-left and literal/literal bitwise expressions, `~`, shifts, computed/nested expressions, trait inference for bitwise operators, aliases/coercions, lowering/runtime semantics, and complete `TypeckResults`.

### IR-778: type-check direct left integer literals for flat-local bitwise operators

- **Decision:** Extend the IR-776 `&`, `|`, and `^` form to one direct integer literal on the left and one eligible concrete primitive path on the right. Integer paths constrain the literal's `ι` to their exact type and receive the expression result. `Byte`, `Bool`, `F32`, `F64`, and `Char` paths report `TYPE_MISMATCH` at the path, expecting `I64`, while leaving the literal variable unresolved for a later integer annotation, tail, or body-end default; do not add `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Keep float literals on the left, literal/literal, unresolved numeric paths, aliases, self/forward references, nested/computed forms, `~`, shifts, and unsupported owners gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.2 synthesizes the left integer literal as an integer-literal variable and checks the right path against it; spec/05 §§5.16.2 and 5.16.5 restrict that variable to integer types, preserve it across failed constraints, and default an unresolved variable to `I64`. Reuse the existing literal-variable resolver for exact-type range checking, complete signed spans, pointer-width bounds, and later annotation/tail resolution. `Byte` supports bitwise operations but cannot be inferred from an integer literal, so it receives the same family mismatch as the other non-integer right paths. The operator is not reported unsupported on a failed literal-family constraint because there is no selected concrete left type yet.

- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm all ten integer primitive paths accept each of `&`, `|`, and `^`; fixed-width and wasm32/wasm64 pointer-width boundaries are checked over full signed literal spans; and `Byte`, `Bool`, `F32`, `F64`, and `Char` paths each report only a path-local `TYPE_MISMATCH` expecting `I64`, with later annotation/tail constraints still applied. ### IR-779: type-check unary bitwise NOT on flat-local paths

- **Decision:** Accept direct unary `~` on a plain path to an eligible parameter or preceding immutable local. Support all ten integer primitives and `Byte`, returning the operand type. For `Bool`, `Char`, `F32`, or `F64`, report `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED` over the full unary expression with the message that the primitive has no `BitNot` implementation; recover the local to the operand type so subsequent paths and tail checking continue. A differing supported annotation reports at the whole initializer and recovers the local to the annotation. Keep literal, unresolved numeric local, alias, self/forward, nested/computed, shift, and unsupported-owner shapes gated.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §§6.8.5–6.8.6 and spec/16 §16.6.1 define unary bitwise NOT through `BitNot` for the ten integer primitives and `Byte`, with no implementation for `Bool`, `Char`, or floats. Naming the missing trait makes the unsupported-primitive diagnostic specific, while operand-type recovery follows the existing unary `not` and binary bitwise diagnostic pattern. This slice checks types only; `BitNot` lowering and execution remain future work.
- **Verification:** The first focused CLI pass found that a mismatched local annotation did not recover the unary result to the annotation, causing a duplicate mismatch on the next local. Two hostile reviews found no actionable P0–P3 issues.

Confirm path resolution honors preceding and shadowed bindings and that literal, unresolved, alias, self/forward, nested/computed operands, shifts, and unsupported owners remain gated. Confirm no lowering or runtime behavior is claimed.

### IR-780: type-check direct integer literals under unary bitwise NOT

### IR-782: type-check direct `Byte` right literals for flat-local bitwise operators

- **Decision:** Extend the flat-local path-left `&`, `|`, and `^` forms to a direct `Byte` literal on the right. A `Byte` left path accepts it. Reusing the typed right-literal path avoids integer-literal inference. Existing primitive checking distinguishes built-in same-type mismatch from a missing generic operator-trait implementation: integers and `Bool`/floats get a right operand mismatch, `Bool`/floats additionally get an unsupported-operator diagnostic, and `Char` gets the concrete missing-trait diagnostic without a synthetic mismatch. Recovery to the left type keeps subsequent locals and tail checks compositional.

### IR-783: type-check flat-local shift path pairs

- **Decision:** Accept one `<<` or `>>` initializer over eligible plain paths to parameters or preceding locals. The left type must be one of the ten integer primitives or `Byte`, and the right type must always be `U32`. For a non-`U32` right path, report `TYPE_MISMATCH` at that path and recover the expression to the left type. For `Bool`, `F32`, `F64`, or `Char` on the left, also report `OPERATOR_NOT_SUPPORTED` over the full expression and recover to the left type. Apply annotation checks to that recovered result. Shifts have no operator traits. Gate literals, aliases, unresolved numeric paths, self/forward paths, nested/computed operands, and unsupported owners; leave shift-count range and runtime behavior for later.
- **Reason:** Spec/06 §6.8.5 states that shift amounts are always `U32`, while §6.8.2 places its explicit `U32` check under a primitive branch that excludes `Char`. Follow the shift-specific rule and check every supported primitive RHS, including when the left type is `Char`, `Bool`, or a float. When both operands are invalid, separate diagnostics identify the independent RHS type error and unsupported left operand. Spec/06 §6.8.10 defines no shift traits, so a generic operator diagnostic avoids inventing trait semantics. Recovering to the left type keeps following locals, tail checks, and annotations compositional.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver function_body_type_check_ --locked` passes all 28 focused body-check tests, including both shift operators across ten integer types and `Byte`. Focused `cargo test -p sai_cli --test check_empty_source primitive_shift --locked` passes 6 tests for supported paths, all non-`U32` primitive RHS types, unsupported left types, diagnostic spans/order, annotation and later-local recovery, and gated forms/owners. `cargo test --workspace --locked --quiet`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `sai fmt --check sample`, and `git diff --check` pass. The first CLI test run exposed that batching many function owners in one generated source selected the global `sai check` feature gate; isolating each case per CLI invocation fixed the harness granularity and all focused tests passed. Hostile review requested result-annotation plus alias and unresolved-numeric-path gate regressions; all were added and verified.
- **Review:** **Review required:** Confirm integer and `Byte` left paths accept only a `U32` right path; every other supported primitive right type mismatches at its own path; unsupported left types receive a full-expression operator diagnostic, including alongside a RHS mismatch; annotations and following locals recover from the left type; and gates remain for literals, unresolved paths, aliases, self/forward, nested/computed operands, and unsupported owners. Confirm that `Char` also receives the RHS `U32` check and no fabricated shift trait is named. Confirm no shift-count overflow or runtime behavior is claimed.

### SAMPLE-008: add a multi-module incident triage console

- **Decision:** Add `sample/incident-response-console` as a read-only console over five fixed incidents. Compute priority from severity and customer-impact weights (40/30/20/10 plus 30/20/10/0) and map scores to P1–P4 at 60/45/25. Set first-response targets to 15/30/60/240 minutes. Count an unanswered incident as an SLA breach only after its age exceeds the target; count an answered incident as a breach only when response time exceeds the target. Escalate unanswered P1 incidents immediately to an incident commander and other unanswered overdue incidents to the duty manager; late answered incidents remain breaches but are not active escalations. Keep fixtures, policy thresholds, and reports deterministic and do not page responders or persist changes.

Fixed data keeps the arithmetic reviewable while package resolution, process/WASI, derives, loop, formatting, and module-analysis stages remain incomplete.
