### IR-872: collect module extern-function inventories

- **Decision:** Extend the target-filtered Phase 1 package inventory to direct function declarations inside exact top-level extern blocks. Pair each block's `ItemTreeKind::ExternBlock` entry with exactly one `TopLevelOwnerDescriptor` of kind `ExternBlock`, then pair every direct `ExternFn` child with its `ExternFunctionOwnerDescriptor`. Verify current-snapshot AST IDs and source pointers, declaration and ItemTree order, normalized names, exact enclosing-block identity, and the owner DefPaths before hashing. The canonical symbol path is `<package>/<module-path>.<function-name>` regardless of the foreign import-module string. Fingerprint the declaration while omitting its actual SAI name token.
- **Reason:** Extern functions are module-level symbols of kind `extern_fn`, and §12.7.1 item 3 gives them the enclosing module's ordinary `m.f` path form. The extern block itself creates no symbol or binding. §12.2.4 makes declaration-name omission the rename-stable fingerprint rule. HIR interns same-header extern blocks and same-name child functions with source-order DefPath disambiguators, so both must be validated against the filtered ItemTree before their hashes are trusted.
- **Target filtering:** `@target` applies to the extern block and removes all its functions before inventory collection (§15.11.3). It is not supported on individual `ExternFn` children; a target attribute on a child remains an attribute error and makes coverage incomplete.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Duplicate, missing, extra, wrong-kind or unpaired block/function owners; duplicate AST identities; source, ItemTree, name, order, parent, package, module, ABI/module-header, or source-order DefPath mismatches; parser/lexer recovery; target/attribute errors; and duplicate module-canonical paths make coverage incomplete. Empty valid Wasm blocks contribute no symbols and remain complete. An `extern "C"` block is Stage 7 and always leaves coverage incomplete; unknown ABIs and a Wasm block without its required module string do likewise. Wasm function forms with `async`, generic parameters, `self`, `where`, `borrows`, or a body remain incomplete. Generic parameters are §12.2.1 symbols, so they are not silently omitted under complete coverage: this slice marks a generic extern declaration incomplete rather than emitting incomplete generic children. The collector does not validate resolved boundary-scalar types or connect reconciliation/persistence. WIT and other non-`ItemTree` package symbols remain an unresolved completeness boundary.
- **Review required:** **Hostile review needed.** Confirm the target-filtered `ItemTree` plus exact top-level `ExternBlock` and direct `ExternFunctionOwnerDescriptor` pairing cannot omit or misclassify retained module imports; verify source-order block-header and child-name disambiguators, including same canonical `m.f` collisions across distinct blocks; confirm the import-module name is not part of the SAI symbol path and that fingerprints omit only the SAI declaration name. Check that target filtering is block-scoped; generic omission cannot yield complete coverage; malformed and unsupported Wasm signature forms remain incomplete; and Stage 7 C declarations fail closed. Direct synthetic missing/duplicate/wrong-kind owner and DefPath corruption tests remain absent because the inventory consumes private query-prepared snapshot inputs. The collector covers only target-filtered source `ItemTree` symbols and does not establish the WIT/non-`ItemTree` package boundary required before persistence.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_extern_function_inventory_ --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passed all 4 focused tests. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_ --locked --offline` passed all 79 module-related tests. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** Independent adversarial review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Non-blocking gaps remain: no owner/DefPath corruption fixtures; no raw-identifier, Unicode, or `@import_name` path/fingerprint regression; no target-filtered earlier identical-block disambiguator fixture; and no direct assertion that interface-nested callables/resources stay absent from emitted symbols. The package WIT/non-`ItemTree` completeness boundary remains unresolved.
- **Remaining scope:** Establish immutable WIT/non-`ItemTree` package-symbol coverage, validate signature types in the owning semantic phase, collect any generic extern parameters only if the language later permits them, and keep reconciliation/persistence disconnected until inventory completeness covers every exact package symbol source.

### IR-873: collect authored WIT interface function inventories

- **Decision:** Extend the Phase 1 package inventory with direct standalone function items from the exact authored WIT `Dir` package selected by the package graph. Accept source and hybrid package contracts with a declared `wit` directory; a hybrid without WIT preserves its prior inventory, while artifact packages remain incomplete. Bind the WIT contract, exact selected package version, unit, direct `.wit` VFS snapshot, root package model, view definitions, and source declaration spans before emitting symbols. Use the public path `ns:pkg/iface.function`, with WIT interface names and SAI-normalized member names. Only root-package interface items are considered; dependency-closure symbols are never added.
- **Fingerprint and fail-closed boundary:** The locked WIT parser exposes a function name span but not the full declaration span. Extend the source scanner to locate direct interface-level freestanding function declarations in original snapshot bytes, then require its declaration span and token sequence to match the parsed WIT item. Fingerprints use stable parser-token-kind/text pairs, omit only the function name token text, and exclude comments, docs, and trivia. Invalid or mismatched spans, package/view identity, missing source bytes, unsupported declaration forms, generated views, worlds, resources, shadowed or missing members, artifact packages, and duplicate public paths leave coverage incomplete. No reconciliation or persistence is connected.
- **Reason:** Section 12.2.4 requires declaration-local fingerprints that survive a rename and ignore trivia while changing for signature edits; the parser's name-only span cannot establish that boundary. Re-scanning the exact VFS snapshot provides that proof without trusting inferred child spans. Section 12.2.1 and spec/04 §4.9.1 include WIT items and specify the public WIT path form, while the `WitView` has a distinct internal tagged canonical path that is not the public package-index path.
- **Review required:** Confirm the fail-closed decision for WIT interface/world shells: assign them no canonical symbol IDs until a public path is specified. Spec/04 §4.9.1 specifies `ns:pkg/iface.x` for interface members but no shell path; impl/12 §12.2.1 and N-H-63 require a canonical path for a package symbol. Therefore, emit only WIT members with normative paths and keep the package inventory incomplete until exact package-source coverage is established. This decision concerns WIT shells; local SAI `interface` and `world` declarations remain symbols under their module paths. Also confirm the use of `ns:pkg/iface.function` for direct interface functions, that unsupported/resource/non-function items and incomplete spans block completeness, and that Hybrid packages with authored WIT follow `Dir(P)` while no-WIT hybrids preserve existing inventory. Confirm scanner token kinds remain stable against the locked `wit-parser` token vocabulary and that scanning binds to the same VFS snapshot as the parser-mapped resource/function name spans. This increment does not authorize reconciliation or durable writes.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_wit --locked` passes all 145 tests, including scanner regressions for rename, trivia, sibling-declaration, signature, token-kind, nested delimiters, direct resource/member spans, classification, malformed members, and exact parser-to-source resource matching. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked` passes against the unchanged public `WitMember` API. `cargo test -p sai_driver wit_function_inventory --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passes all 15 focused tests, including exact selected version, source-span validation, closure isolation, shadowed view incompleteness, resource-method exclusion, generated view incompleteness, and source/hybrid handling. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib --locked --offline` passes all 650 tests. The test graph fixture now tracks valid source-only manifests for each package node; without those manifests the isolated transitive-scope test deterministically returned `MissingInput` while projecting its WIT unit.
- **Hostile review:** Independent read-only adversarial review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. It confirmed hybrid `Dir` handling, exact selected version/contract/VFS checks, and the root hybrid regression.
- **Remaining scope:** Continue inventorying supported WIT members with exact public canonical paths and declaration-local fingerprints. WIT interface/world shells remain un-emitted and keep the package inventory incomplete until canonical shell paths are specified; local SAI interface/world symbol collection is unaffected. Establish exact package coverage before connecting reconciliation or persistence.
### IR-874: collect direct trait declaration inventories

- **Decision:** Extend the target-filtered module inventory for direct source `trait` declarations. Pair each `ItemTreeKind::Trait` entry with exactly one `TopLevelOwnerDescriptor` of kind `Trait` by `(FileId, ErasedAstId)`, resolve its typed declaration through the current snapshot's `AstIdMap`, and verify the owner and children against the target-filtered `ItemTree`. Emit the trait, its type/const generic parameters, direct associated type declarations and methods, and each method's type/const generic parameters. HIR lowering gives traits a module `TypeNs` path and direct members source-ordered `AssocType`/`AssocFn` components. Methods may have their own generic parameters, and `Self` is implicit rather than a source-backed generic symbol. Duplicate same-kind member names receive distinct HIR disambiguators but collide at the canonical path, so the collector retains candidate metadata only with incomplete coverage. SAI's grammar distinguishes uppercase associated-type names from lowercase method names.

Trait/inherent impls and interface declarations remain unsupported top-level forms and therefore make coverage incomplete without emitting their symbols or members. This source `ItemTree` collector does not include WIT or other non-`ItemTree` package symbols, does not prove those sources absent, and is not connected to reconciliation or persistence.

Those boundaries were added as collector regressions, along with a negative test for impl and interface symbol leakage. A follow-up hostile reviewer could not be started because the agent thread limit was reached; the parent reviewed the final diff and reported no blocking findings.

Confirm that `Self` is not emitted, trait/inherent impls and interface/WIT members do not leak into this slice, and no unsupported symbols permit complete coverage. Synthetic owner-map and DefPath corruption remain untested because the collector consumes private prepared-snapshot inputs. WIT/non-`ItemTree` symbol completeness, trait/inherent impls, interface members, persistence, and reconciliation remain future work.
- **Remaining scope:** Add trait/inherent impl, interface, and exact-package WIT symbol inventories; establish completeness across all package symbol sources; then consider reconciliation and persistence.

### IR-875: collect local interface and direct function inventories

- **Decision:** Extend the target-filtered module inventory to direct local `interface` declarations and their direct freestanding `fn` children. Pair each `ItemTreeKind::Interface` with exactly one `TopLevelOwnerDescriptor` of kind `Interface` by `(FileId, ErasedAstId)`, resolve the declaration through the current snapshot's `AstIdMap`, and verify direct children against the filtered `ItemTree` in source order. Emit local interfaces at canonical `<package>/<module>.<interface>` paths with kind `interface`; emit direct interface functions as `assoc_fn` children at `<interface-path>.<function>`. Validate each interface and function `DefPath` parent, component, source-order disambiguator, package/module, and hash before emitting. Fingerprint each declaration from its own syntax and actual name token.
- **Reason:** Local interface declarations and their freestanding functions are package symbols under §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4, with paths defined by spec/04 §4.9.1. The existing HIR interface owner identifies the declaration, while interface member DefPaths use the same source-order association path machinery as other direct members. Direct-child matching prevents nested resources and their methods from being misclassified as interface functions.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Missing, duplicate, extra, or wrong-kind interface owners; stale or mismatched AST IDs/source pointers; ItemTree child count, kind, name, pointer, or source-order mismatch; parser recovery or diagnostics; invalid target attributes; unsupported or malformed interface children/functions; wrong DefPath parent/component/disambiguator; duplicate canonical paths; and fingerprint/hash failures make coverage incomplete. Empty interfaces are complete. Direct interface resources, methods, aliases, enums, and other non-function children are not emitted and make coverage incomplete. This slice excludes `extern "C"` and does not include WIT interface functions, package-wide non-`ItemTree` sources, reconciliation, or persistence.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_interface_inventory_ --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passed all 4 focused tests, and `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_ --locked --offline` passed all 89 module-related tests. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_function_inventory_keeps_impls_out_of_trait_slice_and_collects_interfaces --locked --offline -- --nocapture`, `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` also passed on macOS.
- **Review required:** Confirm exact owner pairing and descriptor consumption; current-snapshot AST identity and direct ItemTree child matching; canonical interface and interface-function paths/kinds and source-order disambiguators; name-token fingerprint stability; and malformed, duplicate, invalid-target, and unsupported declarations remain incomplete. Confirm direct interface functions carrying member `@target` predicates remain incomplete because the current ItemTree API does not filter children by target. Confirm empty interfaces can be complete and interface resources/methods/aliases/enums, nested members, and `extern "C"` symbols do not leak into this slice. Synthetic owner-map and DefPath corruption remain untested because the collector consumes private prepared-snapshot inputs. The package-wide WIT/non-`ItemTree` coverage boundary remains unresolved, so this inventory's apparent completeness is not sufficient for reconciliation or persistence.
- **Hostile review:** An independent read-only adversarial review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. It confirmed exact owner/ItemTree pairing, DefPath parent and disambiguator checks, and exclusion of interface resources and nested methods. A direct function sharing a resource method's name and injected private owner/DefPath corruption are not covered by focused fixtures; those seam tests remain a non-blocking gap. The hostile review did not execute tests.
- **Remaining scope:** Inventory interface resources, associated types, enums, and their members in later slices, then establish exact package coverage across WIT and every other symbol source before connecting reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-876: collect local interface resources and direct functions

- **Decision:** Extend the IR-875 local-interface inventory to direct interface `resource` declarations and their direct callable members. Match each resource against the current interface `ItemTree` child and snapshot AST identity, validate its direct member list against source-ordered `AssocFn` entries, and derive the resource `TypeNs` DefPath under the exact interface owner. Emit resources as `resource` at `<interface-path>.<resource>` and every structurally supported direct function as `assoc_fn` at `<interface-path>.<resource>.<member>`. Derive member DefPaths as `AssocFn` children of that resource, with source-order disambiguators among same-name members. This collector does not classify constructor, static, or method roles because role does not change symbol kind or path.
- **Reason:** Spec/04 §4.9.1 assigns interface resources the interface member path and resource methods the additional `.resource.member` path; impl/12 §12.2.1 maps resource declarations to `resource` and resource callables to `assoc_fn`. HIR already uses the same interface `TypeNs` and resource-child `AssocFn` path chain. Deriving and verifying those paths at each parent keeps nested methods distinct from interface free functions and makes duplicate names inspectable while preserving incomplete coverage. Semantic receiver and boundary-type compatibility belongs to `interface_check`; when a declaration has exact syntactic and identity correspondence, inventory retains its symbol and leaves semantic WIT diagnostics to that phase.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** A missing or mismatched current AST pointer/ID, wrong ItemTree kind or child order, missing attribute-validation record, malformed syntax, invalid attribute, unfiltered target predicate, unsupported generic/async/unsafe/body/clause/visibility form, unsupported nested declaration, DefPath/hash mismatch, or duplicate canonical path keeps coverage incomplete. Empty resources are valid and emit only their resource symbol. Unsupported interface records, aliases, enums, associated types, nested non-callable forms, WIT symbols, and `extern "C"` remain excluded. The collector still covers only the target-filtered module `ItemTree`; it does not prove the full package symbol boundary and does not authorize reconciliation or persistence.
- **Review required:** The hostile review confirmed exact resource/interface and function/resource owner pairing, current-snapshot AST identity, source-ordered ItemTree matching, local same-name `AssocFn` order, DefPath parent/component/disambiguator/hash validation, direct-interface and module-level leakage prevention, and semantic boundary-check deferral. A second fixture now combines a resource with a same-named unsupported interface alias to exercise the shared `TypeNs` disambiguator and distinct DefPath hashes. Private owner-map/DefPath corruption remains an untested seam because the collector consumes prepared-snapshot inputs. Before persistence, the package WIT/non-`ItemTree` completeness boundary still needs an immutable proof.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_interface_resource_inventory_ --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passed all 5 focused resource tests, covering root/nested and empty resources, interleaved direct functions, constructor/static/method paths, fingerprints and hashes, duplicate names, shared interface `TypeNs` disambiguators, deferred semantic checks, invalid/malformed attributes, unsupported associated types, and no nested-member leakage. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_ --locked --offline` passed all 94 module-related tests. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** An independent read-only hostile review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. It verified the exact owner/AST/ItemTree/DefPath identity chain, path and hash construction, duplicate-path behavior, fail-closed malformed and unsupported members, and deferred semantic checks. It initially noted a non-blocking missing fixture for a resource colliding with a same-named interface `TypeNs` member; a follow-up review confirmed the new source-order regression exercises that case and checks the emitted resource hash against the second sibling disambiguator. The reviewer independently ran both the focused suite and the targeted regression successfully.
- **Remaining scope:** Add interface records, aliases, enums, associated types, and their members; inventory all package symbol sources; establish the exact WIT/non-ItemTree coverage boundary before connecting reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-877: collect direct local interface type aliases

- **Decision:** Extend the local interface collector to direct plain type aliases, including type and const generic parameters, for root and nested module interfaces. Reuse the alias syntax and generic-parameter checks from the module alias inventory, while pairing each alias against its direct source-ordered interface `ItemTree` child and its current-snapshot `AstIdMap` identity. Since nested interface aliases do not have module-level `TopLevelOwnerDescriptor`s, derive their `TypeNs` DefPaths beneath the exact validated interface owner. Compute the same-name ordinal across all direct interface `TypeNs` members, including resources and currently unsupported type forms, then verify package, exact parent path, name, disambiguator, hash, and actual alias-name-token fingerprint before emitting `<interface-path>.<alias>` with kind `alias`. Emit type/const generic symbols below the alias at `.generic[Name]`. A structurally valid alias with generic parameters and its generic symbols remain inspectable candidates, while the inventory becomes incomplete because WIT forbids generic interface items.
- **Reason:** Spec/03 §3.6 defines aliases as `type X = T` declarations and §3.9 permits aliases as interface members; spec/04 §4.9.1 gives interface members the `<interface-path>.<member>` form. Impl/12 §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4 define alias and generic-parameter symbols and declaration-local fingerprints. HIR lowers direct interface aliases into the shared `TypeNs` namespace beneath the interface owner, so source-order disambiguation must count all same-named TypeNs siblings even when a sibling kind is not yet supported.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Records, enums, refined aliases, associated types, nested unsupported forms, malformed or recovered aliases, missing targets, invalid attributes (including `@target` on an interface member, prohibited by spec/15 §15.11.3), owner/AST/ItemTree/order/name mismatches, path/hash mismatch, duplicate canonical paths, and generic child/fingerprint failures keep coverage incomplete. Generic parameters are still inventoried when their exact child identity/order and DefPaths validate, but `GENERIC_INTERFACE_ITEM` prohibits generic interface items under spec/13 §13.2.2 and impl/16 §16.6.1, so their presence also makes coverage incomplete. A same-named alias and resource both retain candidates with distinct source-order DefPath hashes while their shared canonical path makes coverage incomplete. WIT and other non-`ItemTree` package symbols, extern declarations, reconciliation, and persistence remain disconnected.
- **Review required:** Confirm direct aliases are a sound supported interface subset and generic aliases must not result in complete coverage even when their type/const parameter candidates validate. The judgment is to retain those exact alias and parameter candidates, then mark incomplete with `GENERIC_INTERFACE_ITEM`. This matches the direct interface-function collector's incomplete-coverage treatment; unlike that function path, aliases deliberately retain generic-parameter candidates after exact child identity/order and DefPath validation. `interface_check` remains the diagnostic owner. Confirm interface aliases with `@target` are rejected as invalid member attributes under spec/15 §15.11.3 and do not leak a candidate. Confirm alias target semantic compatibility belongs to `interface_check`; this collector validates recoverable syntax and exact identity, but does not reject semantically WIT-incompatible targets before emitting candidate symbols. Confirm source-order TypeNs disambiguators count resources and unsupported record/enum siblings, and duplicate canonical alias paths must retain candidates while making the inventory incomplete. The source `interface api { type Output: Copy }` triggers `Collection(Lowering(ItemTreeEntryMismatch))` before the inventory collector runs, so it cannot be used to assert an inventory coverage result; this is documented rather than treated as a collector regression. Private prepared-input owner-map and DefPath corruption remain untested seams. No conclusion about WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness is implied.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_interface_alias_inventory_ --locked --offline` passed 3 focused tests for plain root/nested aliases, generic type/const candidates with incomplete coverage, exact owner and DefPath hashes, actual name-token fingerprints, unsupported records/enums/refined aliases, malformed targets, and invalid attributes. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_interface_ --locked --offline` passed 13 interface tests, including same-name alias/resource TypeNs siblings in both source orders; `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_ --locked --offline` passed all 98 module-related tests. The shared alias/resource TypeNs regressions check source-order disambiguators 0 and 1, distinct hashes, and incomplete duplicate canonical coverage. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** An independent read-only review found no actionable P0–P2 issue and confirmed the exact owner/AST/ItemTree/DefPath chain, fingerprint, generic-child validation, shared `TypeNs` helper, and fail-closed duplicate handling. It noted non-blocking gaps for duplicate aliases and a same-named unsupported record/enum shifting a later alias ordinal; the cross-kind resource/alias case is now tested in both source orders. The source-form parser/lowering rejection and invalid `@target` behavior are documented above. A later hostile review identified that generic aliases could still leave coverage `Complete`; the follow-up fix retains verified alias/parameter candidates but marks coverage incomplete with `GENERIC_INTERFACE_ITEM`, as required by spec/13 §13.2.2 and impl/16 §16.6.1. The review's final follow-up confirmed that implementation and tests, and identified a documentation overstatement about retaining generic parameters compared with interface functions; the ledger now explicitly distinguishes those paths.
- **Remaining scope:** Inventory interface records, enums, associated types and their members; resolve WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness before reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-878: collect direct local interface record, field, and generic-parameter inventories

- **Decision:** Extend the direct local interface inventory to record declarations, named fields, and type/const generic parameters in root and nested-module interfaces. Match each record to its direct source-ordered interface `ItemTree` child and current-snapshot AST identity; validate the complete source-ordered merge of record generic parameters and fields, including child kinds, AST IDs/source pointers, names, types, parser diagnostics, and attribute-validation records. Derive each record's `TypeNs` DefPath beneath the exact verified interface owner using the ordinal shared by all same-named interface `TypeNs` children, including aliases, resources, and unsupported type forms. Verify the package, exact parent, terminal component, disambiguator, DefPath hash, and declaration fingerprint using the record's actual name token. Emit fields at `.field[Name]` beneath the verified record path and type/const parameters at `.generic[Name]`, with their own exact parent DefPaths, hashes, and name-token fingerprints.
- **Reason:** Spec/03 §3.9 permits interface records; spec/04 §4.9.1 assigns record members the interface path, fields the tagged `.field[Name]` form, and generic parameters `.generic[Name]`. Impl/12 §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4 define `record`, `field`, and `generic_param` symbols and declaration-local fingerprints. HIR already lowers interface records and their fields/generics beneath the interface owner, and `interface_member_path_disambiguator` accounts for every direct TypeNs sibling. WIT rejects empty records semantically and generic interface items, but those checks remain with `interface_check` (§16.6.1): an empty record stays an inspectable record candidate, while structurally verified generic-record and generic-parameter candidates are retained with incomplete coverage and a `GENERIC_INTERFACE_ITEM` reason. The same semantic boundary applies to incompatible field types. A valid `@derive` record remains incomplete because this inventory does not collect generated impl symbols.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Wrong direct member kind, missing/mismatched current AST pointers or IDs, incomplete or reordered record children, missing field types, invalid or filtered attributes, parser recovery/diagnostics, unresolvable names, unsupported nested children, path/package/parent/component/disambiguator/hash mismatch, or duplicate canonical paths keep coverage incomplete. Malformed or invalid record children do not emit record/field/generic candidates. Duplicate names can retain distinct candidates only under incomplete coverage. Generic and `where`-clause restrictions and empty-record diagnostics are not used to discard structurally valid record symbols. Interface enums and other unsupported member kinds remain excluded. WIT/non-`ItemTree` package symbols, reconciliation, and persistence remain disconnected.
- **Review required:** Confirm the shared TypeNs sibling ordinal for records in the presence of aliases, resources, enums and other unsupported type members; direct ItemTree/source-order and current-snapshot AST pointer checks for the record and all fields/generics; exact parent DefPaths and the field/generic child hashes and name-token fingerprints; root and nested interface paths; and fail-closed handling of parser errors, malformed fields, invalid attributes, and unsupported member kinds. Confirm the semantic division: retain empty-record candidates for `interface_check` to diagnose with `WIT_EMPTY_TYPE`, retain generic candidates but mark coverage incomplete with `GENERIC_INTERFACE_ITEM`, and leave field-type/WIT compatibility to `interface_check`. Confirm valid derive records do not imply complete coverage while their generated impl symbols are missing. The independent hostile review confirmed the source-order/AST/ItemTree identity, TypeNs disambiguation, exact interface and child DefPaths, hashes, name-token fingerprints, and semantic boundary checks. Synthetic owner/DefPath corruption and an independent proof of WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness remain untested and must not be inferred from these tests.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_interface_record_inventory_ --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passed all 4 focused record tests for root/nested interfaces, fields, empty records, generic type/const parameters, actual-name fingerprints, DefPath hashes, collisions with alias/resource/enum TypeNs siblings, and malformed/invalid forms. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_interface_ --locked --offline` passed all 17 interface inventory tests. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib module_ --locked --offline --quiet` passed all 102 module-related tests. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** An independent adversarial review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its scope confirmed direct source-order ItemTree/current-AST identity, shared TypeNs sibling disambiguation across alias/resource/unsupported forms, exact interface parent and nested record/field/generic DefPaths, DefPath hashes and name-token fingerprints, fail-closed malformed/invalid handling, and the semantic boundary that `interface_check` owns empty-record and field-type compatibility diagnostics while generic records retain candidates under incomplete coverage. The reviewer independently passed the 4 focused record tests and 17 interface inventory tests, and `git diff --check 65447bc...HEAD`. Synthetic owner/DefPath corruption and proof of WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness remain documented gaps.
- **Remaining scope:** Inventory interface enums and their variants, associated types and remaining interface members; resolve immutable WIT/non-`ItemTree` package coverage before reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-879: collect authored WIT resources and direct members

- **Decision:** Extend the selected authored-WIT root interface collector to direct resources and their constructor, method, and static members. Reuse the exact selected root `Dir(P)`, package/version, unit, WIT snapshot bytes, parsed package, and selected view checks. Validate `authored_interface_resource_tokens` resource and member sidecars against the parsed item, member names, kinds, source order, and bounded declaration spans without adding span fields to public `WitMember`. Emit each resource as `resource` at `ns:pkg/iface.Resource` and each supported direct callable member as `assoc_fn` at `ns:pkg/iface.Resource.member`. A WIT constructor maps to the SAI view and public path name `new`; use `WitViewEntity::ResourceMember` and its exact definition path for nested member identity and hashes. Canonical paths use the semantic/view resource name, stripping any `r#` SAI source-spelling prefix.
- **Reason:** Spec/04 §4.9.1 defines interface member paths, while spec/13 §13.7.4, impl/12 §§12.2.1/12.2.4, and impl/16 define resource and resource-member identities and declaration-local fingerprints. Scanner sidecars provide exact source provenance where parsed resource members do not expose spans. The view has distinct tagged identities for items and resource members, so checking each entity and internal DefPath prevents accidental promotion of methods to interface functions and provides stable member hashes. Escaped SAI spelling is required in SAI source, but canonical paths use the semantic name.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Missing or mismatched source bytes, scanner/parsed item or member identity/kind/order/span mismatches, unsupported signatures, missing or shadowed view definitions, unsupported WIT declarations, duplicate canonical paths, generated/artifact views, worlds, and dependency-closure content keep coverage incomplete. Exact candidates for supported declarations remain available when a sibling declaration is unsupported. Empty resource declarations emit a resource candidate. Dependency packages are never inventoried by this root-only slice. WIT interface shell IDs remain un-emitted because spec/04 §4.9.1 has no shell canonical-path form; package reconciliation and persistence remain disconnected.
- **Review required:** Confirm the unresolved no-shell-ID scope until a canonical shell path is specified; confirm `resource` and `assoc_fn` kinds and the `.new` constructor path; confirm canonical paths strip `r#` while preserving that escape in SAI source spelling; confirm unsupported members and any symbol-kind omissions block complete coverage even when supported sibling candidates are retained; confirm dependency closure isolation and that selected `Dir(P)` is the authority for source and hybrid packages. This collector does not resolve the full WIT/package symbol boundary or authorize reconciliation/persistence.
- **Verification:** `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test -p sai_driver wit_ --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passed all 118 matching driver tests, including resource and member path/kind/hash/fingerprint checks, empty resources, constructor/static/method mappings, shadowed `new`, unsupported signatures, dependency isolation, and the escaped `%self` canonical-path regression. `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test -p sai_driver --lib --locked --offline --quiet` passed all 674 driver tests. `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test -p sai_wit authored_resource_and_member_provenance_maps_exact_direct_source_declarations --locked --offline -- --nocapture` passed the focused scanner test. `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `rtk git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** Independent read-only hostile review found one actionable P2: reserved WIT resource names such as `%self` retained their `r#` SAI escape prefix in canonical resource/member paths, which fail symbol-index path validation. The implementation now builds both paths from the stripped semantic/view name. The regression asserts `Self` and `Self.read` paths and validates each with `SymbolIndexEntry::new`. Follow-up hostile review confirmed the correction and found no new actionable issues. It also noted non-blocking opportunities for a reversed constructor/static `new` collision order and a commented/attributed multi-member span fixture.
- **Remaining scope:** Inventory the other authored WIT interface item kinds with exact paths and declaration-local fingerprints; determine complete root-package WIT coverage before connecting reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-880: collect direct local interface enum and variant inventories

- **Decision:** Extend the direct local interface collector to enums, variants, named variant fields, tuple payload fields, and type/const generic parameters in root and nested-module interfaces. Require each enum to match its source-ordered interface `ItemTree` child and current-snapshot AST ID/source pointer. Validate the merged source order of enum generic parameters and variants, then validate each variant's exact ItemTree kind, AST identity, name, and payload shape. Reuse the existing interface `TypeNs` component/disambiguator helpers, generic-parameter collector, named-field collector, canonical-path checks, DefPath hashing, and declaration fingerprinting. Emit enum and variant names at `<interface-path>.<enum>` and `<enum-path>.<variant>`; named payloads use `.field[Name]`, while tuple payloads use decimal `.field[index]` components without padding.
- **Tuple payload DefPath decision:** The current HIR `ItemTree` has no child entries for tuple payload types and HIR lowering does not intern their field DefPaths. To satisfy the canonical symbol path and `field` kind required by impl/12 §12.2.1 and spec/04 §4.9.1, synthesize and intern `DefPathData::Field(index)` immediately below the exact verified variant DefPath. Fingerprint the corresponding `ast::Type` syntax without omitting a name token. This is intentionally a narrow collector-owned identity bridge; it does not claim that HIR currently owns tuple-field definitions.
- **Reason:** Spec/03 §3.9 and spec/13 §13.2 define interface enums and their WIT variant restrictions; spec/04 §4.9.1 defines enum, variant, and field canonical paths. Impl/12 §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4 define enum/variant/field/generic-parameter kinds and declaration-local fingerprints. Interface `TypeNs` ordinals must count all same-named direct siblings, including aliases, resources, records, and unsupported member forms, so enum paths share the existing source-order namespace logic.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Missing or mismatched current AST pointers/IDs, wrong ItemTree kinds, reordered or extra generic/variant/payload children, malformed syntax, parser diagnostics, invalid attributes, unusable names, unsupported nested shapes, interning failures, package/parent/component/disambiguator/hash mismatches, and duplicate canonical paths keep coverage incomplete. Structurally valid empty and generic enums retain their enum/variant/parameter candidates under incomplete coverage (`WIT_EMPTY_TYPE` and `GENERIC_INTERFACE_ITEM`). Structurally valid multi-value tuple payloads retain candidates but make coverage incomplete for WIT incompatibility. At the current `IMPLEMENTED_ATTRIBUTE_STAGE = 0`, `@derive` (stage 2) and `@flags` (stage 4) are rejected before inventory; the tests assert that these declarations fail closed without candidates. When those attribute stages are enabled, accepted derives and flags still make coverage incomplete because their generated impl or synthetic associated-function symbols are outside this slice. This inventory does not establish WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness and does not connect reconciliation or persistence.
- **Review required:** Confirm that synthesizing `Field(index)` under the exact enum variant is the correct stable HIR DefPath representation for tuple payloads despite the current `ItemTree`/HIR omission, that index strings are the specified canonical path spelling, and that the payload `ast::Type` is the correct fingerprint unit. `ItemTree` stores no type value for named `VariantField`s or tuple payloads; HIR retains tuple and record payload `Ty` values, but this collector fingerprints same-snapshot AST syntax and compares neither lowered value. Following the existing record collector's source-syntax design, `Complete` here means symbol membership, canonical-path, fingerprint, and DefPath coverage only; it does not prove AST-to-HIR/WIT type-semantic equivalence. `interface_check` remains responsible for type resolution and WIT semantic compatibility. Confirm interface enum `TypeNs` disambiguators count every preceding same-named direct type namespace sibling, variants use the HIR source-order disambiguator, and duplicate variant canonical paths remain candidates only under incomplete coverage. Confirm the semantic split: empty/generic/WIT-incompatible declarations preserve structurally validated candidates for `interface_check`, while malformed syntax and rejected attributes do not leak symbols. Confirm the stage-0 behavior for `@derive` and `@flags`; positive inventory coverage for these later-stage attributes remains unavailable until Phase 1 advances its implemented attribute stage. Synthetic owner-map/DefPath corruption tests and a proof of WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness remain follow-up requirements.
- **Verification:** `module_interface_enum_inventory_` passed all 7 focused tests for root/nested interface paths, variants, named and tuple payload fields, hashes/fingerprints, shared `TypeNs` order, duplicate variants, generic/empty and WIT-incompatible candidates, parser recovery, invalid attributes, stage-gated derive/flags, record-shaped payload fields, name-stable fingerprints, and explicit/empty-tuple discriminant boundaries. Existing `module_interface_record_inventory_` passed 4 tests and `module_interface_alias_inventory_` passed 3 tests after updating now-supported-enum expectations. The complete `sai_driver` library suite passed all 685 tests. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** An independent read-only adversarial review found no actionable P0–P2 findings and one P3 test-precision gap: explicit discriminant fixtures accepted either variant path instead of asserting the exact candidate for each source. The test now pairs each source with its variant name and checks that exact path. The review examined source/AST/ItemTree identity and order, shared `TypeNs` ordinals, variant and payload DefPaths, the collector-owned tuple `Field(index)` DefPath, canonical paths/kinds, hashing/fingerprinting, duplicates, malformed syntax and attributes, and generic/empty/derive/flags boundaries. It called out non-blocking fixture gaps for record-shaped payload fields, rename-stable fingerprints, and empty tuple/explicit discriminants; focused tests now cover these cases. The review also clarified the semantic boundary: `ItemTree` stores no type value for named `VariantField`s or tuple payloads; HIR retains the tuple and record payload `Ty` values, but the collector fingerprints same-snapshot AST syntax and compares neither lowered value. The inventory's `Complete` status does not establish AST-to-HIR/WIT type equivalence; `interface_check` remains responsible for type resolution and semantic compatibility. Stronger semantic equivalence and WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness remain follow-up work.
- **Remaining scope:** Interface associated types are not grammar-supported under spec/03 §3.9; parser-recovered invalid forms remain incomplete. Establish immutable WIT/non-`ItemTree` package-symbol coverage and any stronger semantic type-equivalence invariant before reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-881: collect authored WIT interface enums and cases

- **Decision:** Extend the selected authored-WIT root-interface inventory to direct unit enums and their unit cases. Bind each candidate to the exact selected root `Dir(P)` source snapshot, parsed package item, interface, selected view member, and `WitViewEntity`. The scanner recovers the enum declaration and each case's source-local range and parser-token-kind/text sequence from the original source; it requires the parsed enum name span and ordered case names to match. Fingerprint the enum from its declaration tokens while omitting only the enum name token, and fingerprint each case independently while omitting only that case's name token. Emit enum symbols at `ns:pkg/iface.Type` with kind `enum`, and case symbols at `ns:pkg/iface.Type.Case` with kind `variant`. Validate the internal view `DefPath` separately: the enum must be `Interface/TypeNs`, each case `Interface/TypeNs/Variant`, with the expected names, canonical internal path, disambiguators, and recomputed `DefPathHash`. Strip any SAI `r#` escape when constructing public paths.
- **Reason:** Spec/04 §4.9.1 assigns WIT interface members their `ns:pkg/iface.member` paths, and impl/12 §§12.2.1/12.2.4 define enum/case symbol kinds and declaration-local, rename-stable fingerprints. Impl/16's `WitView` exposes enums and cases as distinct model entities and internal DefPath components. The parser does not retain a full declaration span for each enum case; rescanning the same source snapshot and cross-checking its exact enum name span and ordered case names provides source provenance without expanding the public `WitMember` API. WIT `variant` declarations may carry payloads and remain excluded; they must not be confused with unit `enum` cases.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Unsupported WIT item kinds, payload variants, empty or malformed enum declarations/cases, unsupported declaration forms, scanner/model span or order mismatches, parsed/view member mismatches, missing or wrong-kind `Item`/`Variant` definitions, noncanonical DefPaths, recomputed hash mismatches, unsupported name spellings, and duplicate public paths keep coverage incomplete. Supported enum/case candidates may still be retained when another sibling is unsupported. Only direct enums from the exact selected root package are considered; dependency-closure symbols are never added. Generated or artifact views, missing source snapshots, and package-source coverage outside this root-only slice remain incomplete. This inventory does not claim package completeness and does not authorize reconciliation or persistence.

### IR-882: collect direct authored WIT interface type aliases

- **Decision:** Extend the selected authored-WIT root-interface inventory to direct `type Name = Type;` declarations only. The scanner locates a declaration in the exact selected root `Dir(P)` source snapshot and accepts it only when the parsed item name span, normalized WIT name, interface, and lexical declaration all agree. Then validate the selected view member, `WitViewEntity::Item`, `Alias` kind, and the internal `Interface/TypeNs` DefPath name, disambiguators, canonical serialization, and recomputed hash. Emit the public path `ns:pkg/iface.Type` with kind `alias`, converting the WIT name with the upper-identifier rule and stripping any `r#` prefix. Fingerprint the declaration tokens while omitting only the alias-name token.
- **Reason:** Spec/04 §4.9.1 gives WIT package members the `ns:pkg/iface.x` canonical path and says re-exports keep the defining declaration's path. Spec/13 §§13.8.2–13.8.3 require type aliases to use the upper SAI identifier conversion. Impl/12 §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4 define alias symbol kind and declaration-local fingerprints. The WIT view already represents aliases with internal `TypeNs` paths, which are separate from the public canonical path.
- **Re-export judgment:** A parser model kind alone does not prove authored ownership: an interface `use` re-export can appear as a `WitItemKind::Alias(WitType::Named(...))` as well as `WitItemKind::Used`. This implementation therefore requires the exact source span to select a direct lexical `type Name = ...;` declaration. Both `Used` and aliases sourced from a `use` member are excluded; the latter keep coverage incomplete because no direct declaration matches their span. This resolves the §4.9.1 re-export rule for this slice without assigning a new public path to the re-export.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Missing or malformed source spans, non-direct alias declarations, source/model or view/item/entity mismatches, wrong DefPath package/component/name/disambiguator/canonical serialization, hash mismatch, invalid name conversion, unsupported alias declarations or target types, duplicate public paths, generated/artifact views, missing source snapshots, and unsupported neighboring items keep coverage incomplete. A direct alias is emitted only after all ownership, identity, and path checks pass. WIT dependencies are not added, and this inventory does not establish package-source completeness or connect reconciliation/persistence.
- **Review required:** Confirm the judgement that only source-proven direct aliases create alias inventory entries, including when the parser models a `use` re-export as `Alias(Named(...))`; confirm `Used` items remain out and their original definition keeps the sole canonical path. Confirm upper-name conversion, raw-name normalization, the `ns:pkg/iface.Type` path, `alias` kind, internal `Interface/TypeNs` path, selected package equality, recomputed hash, and fingerprints that omit only the alias's own name. Confirm unsupported model target forms such as maps, futures, streams, and explicit `Unsupported` types do not leak candidates, while interface semantic compatibility remains with `interface_check`. The targeted integration fixture shows a `use` alias normalized to `Alias(Named(...))`; the source-span scanner rejects it and the inventory contains no re-export path. Query-level mutation of prepared view/entity data remains unavailable through the private `RootDatabase` seam. Multiple-file source provenance, duplicate normalized aliases, and adversarial injected view/entity mismatches remain follow-up fixtures. This does not prove WIT/non-`ItemTree` package completeness.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_wit --lib --locked --offline --quiet` passed all 150 library tests. Focused alias scanner tests passed for direct declaration boundaries, attribute/name masking, nested `use` and type-like token exclusion, malformed type expressions, and rename/target fingerprint token stability. Focused driver tests passed for root aliases, source `use` re-export exclusion, unsupported map targets, exact source-span validation, alias TypeNs path/hash rejection (including a correctly rehashed foreign-package path), and the existing enum inventory. `cargo test -p sai_driver --lib --locked --offline --quiet` passed all 691 driver tests. `cargo check -p sai_driver --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** An independent read-only adversarial review found one P2 identity gap: collection recomputed the alias DefPath hash and validated path components but did not require the path's package to equal `view.package`; a same-shaped foreign-package path with its own valid recomputed hash could have been emitted. Collection now fails closed on selected-package mismatch. A regression test constructs that foreign path and matching hash, confirms the hash is otherwise valid, then rejects it by package identity. Review found no other actionable P0–P3 issue or fail-open path. It confirmed the direct declaration scanner skips `use` lists and nested bodies and that `Used` re-exports do not enter alias collection. Non-blocking gaps remain for quoted/multi-file/duplicate-normalized aliases, query-level injected view/entity/path mismatches, and alias target semantic equivalence outside this inventory boundary.

### IR-883: collect direct authored WIT interface records and fields

- **Decision:** Extend the selected authored-WIT root `Dir(P)` inventory to source-proven direct interface `record` declarations and their named fields. The source scanner returns exact declaration/name byte ranges and token-kind/text pairs from the selected source snapshot. The collector binds each record's parser name span and ordered field names to that scan, then validates the selected interface member, `WitViewEntity::Item`, `Struct` kind, and internal `Interface/TypeNs` DefPath. It validates each named field independently against its ordered `WitViewEntity::Field`, `Field` kind, exact parent record DefPath, source-order field disambiguator, canonical serialization, and recomputed hash. Public paths are `ns:pkg/iface.Record` and `ns:pkg/iface.Record.field[name]`, with kinds `record` and `field`. Record and field fingerprints omit only their own declared-name token.
- **Reason:** Spec/04 §4.9.1 assigns WIT interface members and fields their canonical symbol paths; spec/13 §§13.8.2–13.8.3 define record names, field names, and escaped identifiers. Impl/12 §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4 define record/field kinds and name-masked declaration fingerprints. Impl/16 §§16.4.2 and 16.4.8 define the view's `Interface/TypeNs` record and nested `Field` path. `WitField` does not retain source spans, so a scanner sidecar cross-checked against the selected parser model's field order and names is used for source provenance. View type-field semantic equivalence remains outside inventory and belongs to the WIT semantic validation phase.
- **Re-export judgment:** As with IR-882, model classification alone cannot prove a declaration is directly authored: a `use` re-export can present as a selected type-like item. Only an exact lexical `record` declaration matched to the parser's name span is inventoried. `use` re-exports and nested record-shaped syntax are not direct records and do not receive new public record/field paths; their unsupported coverage remains visible.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Missing or stale source snapshots, missing/malformed name spans, scanner failures, record/field source-to-model count/order/name mismatches, partial parser declaration metadata, unsupported record/field types, view member/entity/kind mismatches, missing or foreign-package paths, wrong DefPath parent/component/name/disambiguator/canonical serialization, recomputed-hash mismatches, invalid name conversion, and duplicate public paths leave coverage incomplete. A rejected record emits no record or fields; an independently invalid field path does not prevent other verified fields from being retained. Supported siblings remain available for inspection. Empty records may retain their source-proven record symbol while semantic WIT validation reports the invalid shape. Only direct records in the exact selected root package are included; dependencies, generated/artifact views, variants/flags/worlds, package completeness, type-equivalence, reconciliation, and persistence remain out of scope.
- **Review required:** Confirm that direct source `record` ownership plus matching parser name span and ordered field names is sufficient provenance for the record and each field when `WitField` has no source range; verify field ranges are bounded, source-ordered, and contain exactly their own name token. Confirm the §4.9.1 interpretation that re-exported record aliases keep their original definition identity and do not become direct records. Confirm upper/lower name conversions, raw-name normalization, public paths and kinds, record/field internal DefPath components and disambiguators, selected-package equality, full canonical serialization, recomputed hashes, and own-name-only fingerprint masking. Confirm that retaining an empty record candidate is compatible with semantic invalidity being reported separately, and that one malformed field may be omitted while other independently verified fields remain. Synthetic query-level corruption of prepared view/entity maps remains unavailable through the private `RootDatabase` seam.
