### IR-884: collect direct authored WIT interface variants and cases

- **Decision:** Extend the selected authored-WIT root `Dir(P)` inventory to direct interface `variant` declarations and their ordered unit or single-payload cases. The source scanner recovers the exact declaration and case ranges plus parser-token-kind/text pairs from the selected source snapshot. The collector binds the variant parser name span and the model's ordered case names and payload presence to that scan, then validates the selected view member, parent `WitViewEntity::Item` with `Enum` kind, and each ordinal `WitViewEntity::Variant` with `Variant` kind. It checks that internal paths use `Interface/TypeNs` for the parent and `Interface/TypeNs/Variant` for each case, match the selected view package and exact parent path, use the expected disambiguators and canonical serialization, and reproduce the stored `DefPathHash`. Public paths are `ns:pkg/iface.Outcome` with kind `enum` and `ns:pkg/iface.Outcome.Case` with kind `variant`. Fingerprints mask only the declaration's own variant or case name; case payload tokens remain in the case fingerprint.
- **Reason:** Impl/12 §12.2.1 classifies WIT package items and names the parent declaration kind `enum` and case kind `variant`; spec/04 §4.9.1 gives WIT members `ns:pkg/iface.x` paths and says re-exports keep the defining path. Spec/13 §§13.7.3, 13.8.2–13.8.3, and 13.8.5 establish the SAI view shape, upper-camel case conversion, and direct case scope. Impl/16 §§16.4.1–16.4.3 represent a variant parent as a view enum and each case as an ordinal `Variant` entity with a unit or one-field tuple shape. Impl/12 §12.2.4 requires declaration-local fingerprints that omit only the current declaration's own name token. `WitCase` has no source range, so scanner ranges are joined to the exact parser item name span and model case order rather than expanding the model API.
- **Direct ownership judgment:** Require a lexical direct `variant` declaration in the selected root interface and the parsed name span. A `use` alias, enum case, nested variant-shaped syntax, or type-like source occurrence is not promoted as a new variant symbol. This preserves the rule that re-exports do not create canonical paths and avoids turning nested payload syntax into interface-owned declarations. Name conversion uses the view's upper-identifier rule, and SAI raw-identifier prefixes are stripped only from public paths.
- **Unsupported payload judgment:** An unsupported payload makes coverage incomplete and omits that case, but does not erase the independently verified parent or supported sibling cases. The parent is accepted only when the model's aggregate unsupported marker agrees with the presence of unsupported case payload shapes and the selected view member carries that same marker. If declaration ownership/order, source/model payload-presence, or parent identity cannot be established, the entire variant is rejected. A bad case entity/path/hash affects only that case candidate.
- **Semantic boundary:** The scanner proves exact same-snapshot source provenance, source-ordered names, and payload presence. It does not independently parse payload types to prove semantic equivalence with `WitType`; payload syntax still changes the fingerprint, while `interface_check` owns WIT type resolution and compatibility. This slice does not claim package completeness and does not connect reconciliation or persistence.
- **Corrective change:** Hostile review found that the parent `Outcome` was emitted as `SymbolKind::Variant` even though §12.2.1 assigns `enum` to the parent and `variant` to its cases. The parent is now emitted and fingerprinted as `SymbolKind::Enum`; case candidates remain `SymbolKind::Variant`. The integration assertion checks both classifications. Reverification passed the focused `wit_variant_inventory_collects_payload_cases_and_keeps_supported_siblings` test, all 699 `sai_driver` library tests, `cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check`.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** Missing/stale source, malformed declaration/case syntax, empty or unsupported scanner forms, source/model count/order/name/payload-presence disagreement, unsupported name conversion, inconsistent unsupported metadata, missing or conflicting selected view member/entity/kind, duplicate public paths, foreign-package paths, wrong internal path parent/component/name/disambiguator/canonical serialization, or a recomputed hash mismatch leave coverage incomplete. Only direct variants in the exact selected root package are considered; dependencies, generated/artifact views, enum declarations, re-exports, nested forms, and other unsupported WIT item kinds remain excluded or incomplete.
- **Review required:** **Hostile review needed.** Confirm the single-payload case scanner boundary and source token masking; that matching the item span plus case names/order/payload presence is sufficient source-to-model binding without separately equating parsed payload types; and that an unsupported payload should retain the parent and other supported case candidates while remaining incomplete. Confirm the public parent path `ns:pkg/iface.Outcome` has kind `enum` and the case path `ns:pkg/iface.Outcome.Case` has kind `variant`, plus selected package equality, parent/case DefPath components, case ordinal mapping, disambiguators, canonical strings, and recomputed hashes. Confirm that scanner rejection of an ambiguous/malformed declaration must invalidate all its cases, while a later per-case view/path failure may preserve verified siblings. Query-level mutation of the private prepared-view/entity seam, multi-file root source, quoted names, and duplicate SAI-normalized-name forms remain untested. Full root-package WIT coverage and any semantic-equivalence evidence are still required before persistence; reconciliation and persistence remain disconnected.
- **Verification:** `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_wit --lib --quiet` passed all 156 tests. `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --lib --quiet` passed all 699 tests. Focused variant driver tests passed source identity, payload-presence/order checks, view path/hash predicates, disambiguators, and the supported-sibling integration fixture. The full driver run first exposed IR-883's stale expectation that this newly supported variant was absent; its record-only fixture was narrowed so the two inventory slices remain independently tested. `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_driver`, `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `rtk git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** Pending independent adversarial review. Record findings and corrective changes here before declaring the slice ready.
- **Remaining scope:** Continue with the remaining direct authored WIT interface item kinds and exact package symbol sources while keeping unsupported or ambiguous forms incomplete. Establish immutable root-package WIT coverage before reconciliation or durable persistence.

### IR-885: collect direct authored WIT interface flags

- **Decision:** Extend the selected authored-WIT root `Dir(P)` inventory to direct interface `flags` declarations. Emit the parent at `ns:pkg/iface.Flags` as kind `enum`. Emit one constant per validated flag at `ns:pkg/iface.Flags.Flag`, kind `const`; the name is converted to upper camel case. Bind the parsed parent name span and ordered `WitFlags.flags` list to exact direct scanner ranges, then validate the selected `WitViewEntity::Item`/`WitViewDefKind::Enum`, selected package, parent `Interface/TypeNs` path, disambiguator, canonical serialization, and recomputed DefPath hash.
- **Reason:** Impl/12 §12.2.1 maps WIT flags parents to `enum` and spec/13 §13.9.4 makes each `F.X` a nameable constant. Spec/04 §4.9.1 gives the constant path `ns:pkg/iface.F.X` and keeps re-exports at their defining paths. Spec/13 §§13.7.3, 13.8.2–13.8.3, and 13.9.4 define the view, name conversion, and flag bit semantics. Impl/16 §§16.4.1–16.4.3 and 16.9.2–16.9.4 describe the enum-like parent, ordered flags, and constants. The view allocates no flag-constant `DefId` or `VariantDef`; the inventory derives its stable identity from the verified parent view `DefPath` plus a `ValueNs(flag)` child and computes its hash with `DefPathHash::compute`.
- **Fingerprint and ordering:** The parent fingerprint masks only its own name and retains all ordered flag names. Each constant fingerprint masks the flag's own name token and appends the stable token pair `("WitFlagsBitIndex", <zero-based bit index>)`. The inventory-only `ValueNs(flag)` component uses disambiguator zero because each flag name is unique (impl/02 §2.8.2). Reordering flags therefore changes the constant fingerprint but preserves the name-based `DefPathHash` and symbol identity, even when the public canonical path is unchanged. This derived path is a deliberate inventory rule for source constants without view `DefId`s; it does not claim that the compiler allocated such a definition.
- **Ownership and limits:** Only lexically direct flags declarations in the selected root interface are considered. `use` members and flags-shaped nested text are not promoted; no synthetic `empty`, `all`, `contains`, or `is_empty` `FlagsMethod` is a source symbol. Empty, exact or case-insensitive duplicate-name, malformed, or unsupported direct flags forms yield incomplete coverage and no parent or constant candidates for that declaration; independently verified supported siblings may remain. A duplicate after SAI name conversion also rejects the whole declaration before candidate emission. A declaration over 32 flags may retain its source- and view-verified parent `enum` candidate but emits no constant candidates and leaves coverage incomplete, because the invalid type has no accepted flags bit semantics. The local SAI `@flags enum` source inventory is a separate path and remains incomplete; it is not converted from variant candidates to constants in this slice. Current semantic flags-constant resolution is not linked to the inventory symbols; reconciliation, persistence, package completeness, and reference linking remain out of scope.
- **Hostile-review correction:** Review found that treating the flags parent as the only symbol omitted the constants explicitly defined by spec/13 §13.9.4. The collector now emits validated direct flag constants and tests their public paths, kinds, derived path hashes, masked fingerprints, and reordering behavior. It does not fabricate a `VariantDef` or `WitViewEntity::Variant`.
- **Identity correction:** Hostile review found that unique flag names must use the standard zero disambiguator (impl/02 §2.8.2). Each `ValueNs(flag)` path component now uses disambiguator zero; the bit index stays in the fingerprint. The reorder test verifies that the named constant hash remains stable while its fingerprint changes.
- **Collision correction:** Independent review found that case-insensitive duplicate WIT names could normalize to one SAI constant path while still leaking the parent and first constant as partial candidates. The scanner now rejects case-insensitive duplicate flag names, and the driver preflights canonical SAI constant names before emitting any candidates for the declaration.
- **Review required:** **Hostile re-review needed.** Confirm that flag constants are kind `const` at upper-camel `ns:pkg/iface.F.X` paths and that no flag is modeled as a variant. Review the inventory-only `ValueNs(flag)` path extension with zero disambiguator against the view's lack of constant `DefIds`; verify the name-based hash remains stable while the fingerprint changes on reordering. Confirm that a valid 1–32 flag declaration emits every distinct normalized constant, while empty and over-limit declarations emit no constants (empty emits no parent; over-limit may retain the parent) and remain incomplete. Check that exact and case-insensitive duplicate WIT names, and any canonical-name collision, suppress the entire declaration's parent and children while preserving verified sibling declarations. Check malformed/nested/`use` source boundaries and that synthetic methods remain excluded. Local SAI `@flags enum` inventory and semantic-use-to-symbol linking are explicitly not covered. Mutations of private prepared-view/entity inputs and full root-package WIT coverage remain outside this slice.
- **Verification:** `sai_wit` focused `flags_scanner` tests passed 2/2; focused `sai_driver` `wit_flags_` tests passed 4/4. Full `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_wit --quiet` passed all 160 tests and `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --quiet` passed all 705 tests. `cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. The over-limit fixture uses SAI-convertible WIT names so it isolates only the 32-flag semantic limit.
- **Hostile review:** Independent adversarial review of `0d3caed` and the full branch diff found no actionable P0–P3 issues. Review confirmed that ASCII case folding matches spec/13 §13.8.1 for valid WIT identifiers and that the driver rejects conversion failures and canonical-name collisions before emitting any candidates. Focused flag tests passed 4/4; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The integration fixture exercises case-insensitive duplicates at the scanner gate; the driver's additional post-conversion collision branch was verified by inspection.
- **Remaining scope:** Implement local SAI `@flags enum` constant inventory, link semantic `FlagsConst` references to these symbols, continue direct authored WIT interface items, and establish an immutable proof of every root-package symbol source before connecting reconciliation or durable persistence.

### IR-886: construct validated local flags descriptors

- **Decision:** Add a private `FlagsDef` and `FlagsRepr` representation builder in `sai_ty::iface` for interface-local `@flags enum` declarations. Preserve source declaration order as `(Symbol, Span)` pairs and choose `U8`, `U16`, or `U32` for 1–8, 9–16, or 17–32 flags. Keep empty declarations as `Ok(None)` so the existing `WIT_EMPTY_TYPE` diagnostic remains authoritative. For invalid non-empty declarations, report one `INVALID_FLAGS_ENUM` using the existing precedence: first payload, then first explicit discriminant, then the 33rd name. Call the builder from the existing flags diagnostic path without changing feature gates.
- **Reason:** Impl/16 §16.9.1 assigns flags validity and invalid-enum fallback to `adt_def`; §16.9.2 defines declaration order and representation width. A small typed builder gives the current temporary validation path one tested representation contract before the real `adt_def` query exists.
- **Scope boundary:** A valid descriptor is currently discarded after validation because local `adt_def` storage and `flags_def` queries are not implemented. This is a staging foundation, not a completed flags type, symbol inventory, `F.X` resolution, generated-method implementation, or Stage 4 feature. No `VariantDef` identity or bit-index-based symbol identity is chosen here.
- **Review required:** Confirm that empty flags remain ordinary empty enums; payload, discriminant, and count invalidity retain the documented precedence and source span; the 1/8/9/16/17/32 boundaries select the expected width; declaration order and source spans remain paired; and the builder's valid result is not presented as an active type/query until `adt_def` consumes it. Decide and review local flag-constant DefPath identity, fingerprint/reordering semantics, and synthetic-method inventory before implementing semantic references.
- **Verification:** `cargo test -p sai_ty` passed all 69 unit tests, including flags representation boundaries, ordered names/spans, empty declarations, and invalid payload/discriminant/count cases. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. Tests used the installed Rust 1.99.1 toolchain through explicit `RUSTC`, `RUSTDOC`, and `RUSTFMT` paths because the local `mise` shim had no configured Rust version; generated per-worktree build artifacts were removed.
- **Hostile review:** Independent review confirmed invalidity precedence, empty-enum behavior, representation boundaries, and the staging boundary. It found that public descriptor fields allowed callers to construct values that bypassed validation; `FlagsDef`, `FlagsRepr`, and their fields are now private until a validated consumer exists. The 69 `sai_ty` tests and formatting check passed again after this fix.
- **Remaining scope:** Integrate validated descriptors into local `adt_def` and `flags_def`, then add name-based flag constants and semantic `FlagsConst` resolution without broadening the feature gate prematurely.

### IR-887: collect module enum tuple-payload field symbols

- **Decision:** Extend the root and nested module enum inventory to emit one `field` symbol for each structurally valid tuple payload type. Keep unit variants and named record payload behavior unchanged. Emit payload `i` at `<enum-path>.<variant>.field[i]`, preserving source order and checking each payload `Type` CST node for recovery or parser errors before adding candidates.
- **Identity judgment:** The current `ItemTree`/HIR has no child field declaration or per-payload `DefId` for tuple variants. Synthesize an inventory-only `DefPathData::Field(Symbol(decimal_index))` under the exact verified variant `DefPath`, with disambiguator zero, then compute the normal `DefPathHash`. Fingerprint the corresponding same-snapshot `ast::Type` syntax node as a `field` declaration without masking a name token. This makes tuple position the identity component and payload type syntax the fingerprint input; it does not claim HIR allocated a field definition.
- **Reason:** Impl/12 §12.2.1 includes tuple-variant payloads as `field` symbols, §12.2.4 requires each candidate's DefPath hash and fingerprint, and spec/04 §4.9.1 fixes the public `.field[i]` path and unpadded decimal index spelling. The existing interface enum inventory already applies the same collector-owned identity bridge; this slice brings local module enums into parity without expanding HIR's data model.
- **Fail-closed coverage:** The existing exact enum/variant source-pointer, AST ID, ItemTree kind/order, parent path, and target checks run before tuple field emission. A malformed tuple type, parser diagnostic, unexpected ItemTree children, interning/hash/path error, or duplicate canonical path leaves coverage incomplete. Invalid tuple declarations do not leak partial payload fields. Derived enums and other unsupported declarations remain incomplete under their existing rules. `Complete` here proves candidate membership, path/hash identity, and syntax fingerprint coverage; it does not prove AST-to-HIR type equivalence, type resolution, WIT compatibility, or symbol-query integration.
- **Review required:** Confirm that synthesizing `Field(index)` beneath the exact variant is the correct stable identity although `ItemTree`/HIR has no per-payload `DefId`; that index identity intentionally follows payload position when tuple members are reordered; and that the `ast::Type` node is the correct fingerprint unit. Confirm zero disambiguators and decimal index spelling match the canonical path contract. The collector does not compare the syntax type with the lowered `Tuple` payload `Ty`; semantic type resolution remains outside this inventory slice.
- **Verification:** The focused `module_enum_inventory_` suite passed 8 tests, the broader module-inventory selection passed 111 tests, and the complete `sai_driver` library suite passed all 707 tests. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** An independent read-only adversarial review found no actionable code defects. It verified AST/ItemTree identity checks precede tuple enumeration, payload order is preserved, malformed syntax fails closed, and the synthesized DefPaths and fingerprints match the recorded rule. It independently raised the `Field(index)` identity and syntax-fingerprint boundaries captured under Review required.
- **Remaining scope:** Add local enum tuple fields to any future semantic queries only when that query has an explicit tuple-field contract; keep HIR changes separate from this inventory-only bridge.

### IR-888: harden authored WIT source provenance tests

- **Decision:** Add regression coverage for root WIT declarations whose source spans are ambiguous without their file identity, escaped `%type`/`%enum` names, direct type aliases versus `use` aliases and nested record fields, and case-insensitive duplicate flags that would also share a converted SAI constant spelling. The duplicate declaration emits no partial flags candidates while an unrelated valid sibling remains selectable.
- **Reason:** The source scanner and parser expose complementary views of WIT: parser spans are local to a file, while scanner provenance establishes which authored declaration those spans identify. Tests use two root files with identical local declaration-name ranges and assert both the selected path and exact source slice; selecting the other file fails the expected-path and declaration-content assertions. Directness tests prevent an alias-shaped use or nested field from being promoted into an authored interface type.
- **Fail-closed behavior:** The existing collector treats invalid or ambiguous source identity and scanner/parser disagreement as incomplete without leaking partial candidates. This PR adds regressions for exact root-file mapping, non-direct alias syntax, and case-insensitive duplicate flags; it does not add a scanner/parser-disagreement test. It also does not establish full root-package WIT coverage or exercise the driver's separate post-conversion collision branch.
- **Review required:** Confirm that declaration identity requires both the exact root source file and the local byte range; escaped WIT identifiers retain their semantic name while mapping to their precise source token; only direct declaration syntax contributes candidates; and scanner-level duplicate flags reject the whole declaration without suppressing valid siblings. The driver post-conversion canonical-name check is defense in depth: the scanner rejects case-insensitive duplicates first, and WIT name conversion is injective for valid names in a scope, so valid authored WIT cannot reach that branch. Direct branch coverage would require a private seam with explicitly synthetic invalid provenance.
- **Verification:** Focused multi-file provenance coverage passed 1 test; focused scanner rejection coverage passed 3 tests; all 163 `sai_wit` library tests passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** Independent read-only review confirmed the tests assert exact source slices and file paths, distinguish direct declarations from aliases and nested fields, and preserve valid sibling flags. It found and prompted correction of terminology that called percent-escaped identifiers “quoted”; no actionable defects remained after the correction.
- **Remaining scope:** Test the defensive driver post-conversion branch only if a minimal private helper can do so without claiming valid-WIT reachability; broader WIT completeness and reconciliation remain separate work.

### IR-889: carry validated local flags descriptors into WIT generation

- **Decision:** Return a typed `InterfaceItemCheck` containing both diagnostics and an optional opaque `FlagsDef`. For a valid, accepted local `@flags enum`, pass that descriptor through the current interface-use pass into generated WIT. Verify that the descriptor's type owner, ordered flag symbols and spans, unit shapes, and omitted discriminants still match the current HIR enum; fail closed on a mismatch. Generate `WitItemKind::Flags` from the descriptor's ordered symbols. Keep `IMPLEMENTED_ATTRIBUTE_STAGE` at 0.
- **Reason:** The existing WIT generator consumes the same accepted interface declaration and is the earliest real downstream consumer of validated declaration order. Carrying the descriptor locally makes WIT output use the same validated names and binds that output to the exact HIR owner without introducing a parallel lookup API.
- **Scope boundary:** This transient handoff is not `adt_def(DefId)` or `flags_def(DefId)`, and does not store a descriptor in a query result. It does not add `AdtDef`, semantic `Ty`, local flag constants, type-relative `FlagsConst` resolution, generated methods, or Stage 4 attribute support.
- **Review required:** Confirm that the direct WIT generator is a suitable temporary consumer before the real `adt_def` query exists; that passing the check result in the same owner iteration is not a substitute query; that owner/name/span/shape checks prevent stale or cross-wired descriptors; and that descriptor order controls emitted WIT flags. Confirm that invalid or empty accepted markers cannot reach generation and that Stage 0 remains unchanged. The driver-level regression test directly exercises the accepted-marker checker and conversion helper because the Stage 0 gate prevents ordinary source input from reaching Stage 4 `@flags`.
- **Verification:** `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib` passed all 70 tests, including descriptor retention, representation boundaries, source-order bindings, empty/invalid declarations, and stale-owner/source rejection. `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 708 tests, including descriptor-to-WIT order and fail-closed cases. `cargo test --workspace --locked --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** The first independent review found one P2 coverage gap: no driver test exercised descriptor-to-WIT conversion while `@flags` remained gated. The initial direct conversion-helper test was also judged to bypass the generator's marker/descriptor selection. The generator now delegates that selection to the tested `generated_interface_enum_wit_item_kind` helper. A second independent review confirmed coverage for accepted matching flags, missing or mismatched descriptors, unmarked enum selection, unexpected descriptors, and empty declarations; it found no remaining actionable issues.
- **Remaining scope:** Build the semantic ADT model and tracked `adt_def`/`flags_def` queries, then implement local flag constants and type-relative resolution in separate slices.

### IR-890: inventory local SAI flags enum cases

- **Decision:** When the interface semantic checker accepts a local `@flags enum` with 1–32 uniquely named unit cases and no explicit discriminants, emit each case in the module function inventory as a `const` at `<enum-path>.<case>`. Reuse the validated HIR variant's existing `VariantDef` path and DefPathHash for identity; do not synthesize a second definition. Fingerprint the case declaration while masking its own name and append a typed `LocalFlagsBitIndex` token pair so declaration order changes the constant value fingerprint. Renaming a case changes its path hash while preserving the name-masked fingerprint; reordering cases preserves their path hashes while changing the bit-index-sensitive fingerprints. Invalid, empty, ambiguous, or unsupported shapes do not emit flag constants and instead follow the ordinary-enum inventory path where that path can be represented.
- **Reason:** Spec/13 §13.9.4 defines the local flags source shape, declaration-order bit positions, and invalid-shape fallback. Impl/12 §§12.2.1 and 12.2.4 require the flags case symbol kind and name-masked declaration fingerprints; impl/16 §§16.9.1 and 16.9.3 define descriptor validation and the pending local inventory slice. The HIR already supplies stable variant identity for each case, so reusing its verified path preserves rename behavior and avoids claiming that a separate DefId exists.
- **Diagnostic and fallback judgment:** The inventory does not broaden flags validity rules. Duplicate source case names prevent ambiguous canonical candidate emission but are not, by themselves, represented as a new `INVALID_FLAGS_ENUM` diagnostic in this slice. An explicit discriminant is treated as flags-invalid and falls back to ordinary enum candidates; it is not independently reported as `WIT_EXPLICIT_DISCRIMINANT` for a flags declaration. Payload, empty, and over-limit declarations likewise do not become flag constants. Coverage remains incomplete when generated flags methods are absent from the inventory.
- **Scope boundary:** `IMPLEMENTED_ATTRIBUTE_STAGE` remains 0, so ordinary source programs still receive the existing unsupported-attribute gate. This change does not add `AdtDef`, `flags_def`, local `FlagsConst` resolution, generated methods, or a claim of complete symbol coverage. A `#[cfg(test)]`-only collection seam accepts the marker after the production Stage 0 filtering so the real collector can be exercised end to end without altering production behavior.
- **Review required:** Confirm that verified HIR `VariantDef` identity is the correct DefPath identity for `const` cases; renaming changes the canonical path and DefPathHash while preserving the name-masked fingerprint, whereas reordering preserves each case path hash and changes the bit-index-sensitive fingerprint. Confirm that only valid 1–32 case unit enums without explicit discriminants are classified as flags; invalid shapes never leak const candidates; duplicate-name fallback is kept distinct from diagnostic validity; and the `INVALID_FLAGS_ENUM` versus `WIT_EXPLICIT_DISCRIMINANT` distinction matches the flags checker. Confirm that generated methods correctly keep coverage incomplete and that the test-only Stage 4 acceptance seam is absent from non-test builds.
- **Verification:** Focused flags fingerprint, HIR attribute, and driver inventory tests passed. `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_semantic`, `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_hir`, and `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver` passed, including all 711 driver tests and end-to-end checks for valid constants, invalid-shape fallback, real variant DefPathHash behavior, renames, and reorder-sensitive fingerprints. `cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_driver`, `cargo test --locked --offline --workspace`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed using the installed Rust 1.99.1 toolchain.
- **Hostile review:** Independent adversarial review first identified missing positive collector coverage behind the unchanged Stage 0 gate and a diagnostic-precedence mismatch for explicit discriminants. These were corrected with actual collector tests and flags-specific fallback diagnostics. A second review verified the real collection path, invalid-shape fallback, real DefPathHash rename/reorder behavior, duplicate-name/diagnostic distinction, and Stage 0 boundary; its remaining test-seam hygiene note was resolved by compiling the acceptance seam only under `cfg(test)`. No actionable behavior defect remains.
- **Remaining scope:** Implement `AdtDef` and `flags_def` queries, then resolve type-relative `FlagsConst` references and account for generated methods before claiming complete local flags semantics or inventory coverage.

### IR-891: add a snapshot-bound local flags ADT projection

- **Decision:** Add `sai_ty::adt::LocalFlagsAdtDef` as the first semantic ADT model, limited to validated local flags declarations. It represents `AdtKind::Flags` with one synthetic variant and one private integer `bits` field whose type follows the validated `FlagsDef` representation (`U8`, `U16`, or `U32`). Carry these values in the existing package `interface_uses` derived-query memo and include their canonical DefPath hashes, model shape, representation, declaration-ordered flag names, and source locations in its stable fingerprint. Expose lookup only through `Phase1PackageScopesCollection::local_flags_adt_def(snapshot, owner)`, which rejects any workspace snapshot other than the collection's exact snapshot. Keep `IMPLEMENTED_ATTRIBUTE_STAGE` at 0 and the accepted-marker collection seam test-only.
- **Reason:** `FlagsDef` already validates source owner, ordered unit-case names and spans, omitted discriminants, count limits, and representation. Building the small ADT projection beside that same-snapshot validated descriptor keeps the owner binding exact without inventing a general type query or changing production feature gates. The source package's append-only `DefPathInterner` supplies distinct real child `LocalDefId`s for reserved non-identifier `$flags` and `$bits` path components. The exported constructor verifies that owner and children resolve in the supplied interner, that the owner is a type path, that the child paths are exactly owner → `Variant($flags, 0)` → `Field($bits, 0)`, and that the supplied symbols have the reserved spellings; the driver independently checks these conditions before exposing the model.
- **Fallback and scope boundary:** Invalid or empty flagged enums receive no `LocalFlagsAdtDef` and remain ordinary enum declarations for existing checking and inventory behavior. This API is not the complete `adt_def(DefId)` or `flags_def(DefId)` contract: it does not classify other local ADTs or imported WIT view flags, provide general field/type semantics, resolve type-relative `FlagsConst`, or model generated flags methods. Absence from this collection is not proof that an arbitrary definition is not an ADT.
- **Review required:** Confirm that a flags-only public model and lookup on the existing package-level derived query are an acceptable first semantic slice; neither should be mistaken for a dedicated general `adt_def` query. Confirm that `$flags` and `$bits` are suitable reserved synthetic path names, that their actual DefPath children are preferable to aliased owner IDs, and that zero disambiguators are stable for each single synthetic child. Confirm the constructor independently rejects children from other packages/interner sessions, wrong parent paths, nonzero disambiguators, and non-reserved variant/field names. Confirm that exact snapshot rejection is the right public stale-result behavior and that the fingerprint includes every observable flags descriptor value, including canonical source path/package and range for each exposed flag span. Confirm that the Stage 0 gate and ordinary-enum fallback stay unchanged and that omission of WIT-view flags is explicit.
- **Verification:** `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib` passed all 74 tests, including representation boundaries and constructor ownership/path/name checks. Focused driver fingerprint movement coverage passed, and `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 714 tests, including DefPath/owner, snapshot-rejection, stable-fingerprint, and invalid/empty fallback cases. `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_driver`, `rtk mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `rtk git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** The first independent review found a P2 public-constructor invariant gap: package-equal child IDs from another interner or unrelated paths and ordinary spellings could enter the ADT model. The constructor now validates the supplied `DefPathInterner`, exact owner/child paths and reserved spellings; tests cover same-package foreign interner IDs, a wrong parent path, a different-package interner and IDs, and visible variant/field names. The reviewer also found a P3 fingerprint gap because flag spans are observable through `flags_def()` but not hashed. The fingerprint now includes each flag's canonical source path/package and range, and a relocation regression verifies the change. The follow-up review confirmed both fixes and found no P0–P2 behavior defect, then identified a P3-only test gap for nonzero child disambiguators; regressions now verify nonzero variant and field disambiguators are rejected. The final follow-up review confirmed the disambiguator/name cases and found no remaining P0–P3 findings. Remaining API scope is limited to local validated flags, not general ADT queries or imported WIT views.
- **Remaining scope:** Add general local `adt_def` coverage for records, enums, distinct/refined types, and resources; then add the exact `flags_def` query semantics and imported WIT view support before implementing type-relative flag constants or generated methods.

### IR-892: project local interface unit enums into the partial ADT model

- **Decision:** Extend `sai_ty::adt` with `AdtKind::Enum`, fixed-width integer discriminant types, and `LocalUnitEnumAdtDef`. Extend the existing snapshot-bound package `interface_uses` result with `LocalInterfaceEnumAdtProjection::{Flags, Unit, Unsupported}` for every local interface enum owner encountered by that same-snapshot HIR pass. Unit enums preserve declaration order and real HIR variant DefIds after checking their package and canonical parent/variant DefPaths; implicit discriminants start at zero and continue by one, while explicit unit-enum discriminants are retained. The default discriminant type is I64. The public unit-enum constructor accepts HIR plus an `InterfaceItemCheck`, validates unit shape and discriminants itself, and requires the check to match the enum's captured source identity and raw `@flags` validity. The `Phase1PackageScopesCollection` lookup rejects a different workspace snapshot. Keep the Stage 0 `@flags` gate and its test-only marker acceptance seam unchanged.
- **Reason:** The existing `interface_uses` collection already lowers each filtered local interface member against the snapshot used to build package scopes and validates its nominal owner identity. Building this small projection beside that result preserves the source identity without inventing synthetic variant DefIds or introducing a general query before semantic type lowering is ready. `Unsupported` distinguishes encountered generic or payload enums from a missing projection, and `None` remains limited to owners that are not local interface enums in this subset.
- **Fallback and scope judgment:** Valid accepted local flags continue to use `LocalFlagsAdtDef` and report a `Flags` projection. Empty or invalid `@flags` unit enums use the ordinary unit-enum model when their discriminants are representable; this includes malformed marker arguments, while a syntactically valid raw marker on a valid flags-shaped enum cannot be suppressed by passing `false` to the public checker. Payload variants, generic parameters, raw `@repr`, malformed discriminants, overflow, out-of-range values, duplicate discriminants, and failed enum checks produce explicit unsupported reasons. A raw interface `@repr` is not trusted as a discriminant representation, even though the enum type remains structurally visible. This API covers local interface enums only; module enums, records, distinct/refined types, resources, imported WIT types, and general `adt_def(DefId)`/`flags_def(DefId)` queries remain outside this slice. Payload semantic types are deferred until type/HIR conversion in impl/03 §§3.5.1–3.5.7 and §3.6.1.
- **Fingerprint judgment:** Include each projection kind, owner and variant canonical DefPath hash, unit-enum discriminant type and ordered variant names/discriminants in the existing stable interface-use fingerprint. Fingerprinting the stored semantic projection makes snapshot memo equality agree with its externally observable result while retaining rename-stable canonical identity and order-sensitive enum contents.
- **Review required:** Confirm that the local interface enum projection belongs on the package `interface_uses` result until a real semantic `adt_def(DefId)` query can consume the completed type-conversion layer; confirm that the accessor's `None` semantics do not imply a non-ADT classification. Confirm that default I64 plus integer `@repr` support is the right narrow boundary: this slice uses I64 for ordinary unit enums and returns explicit `Unsupported(UnvalidatedRepresentation)` for raw interface `@repr` instead of trusting an unvalidated attribute. Confirm that unit enums retain explicit and implicit values in declaration order, that range and uniqueness rejection is appropriate before full semantic diagnostics are implemented, and that empty/invalid `@flags` unit enums follow ordinary-enum fallback while payload `@flags` enums remain unsupported. Confirm that a caller-provided checker boolean cannot route a syntactically valid flags-shaped raw declaration into `Unit`, while malformed/empty markers still retain the documented fallback. Confirm valid flags stay `Flags`, Stage 0 behavior is unchanged, and test-only marker acceptance cannot leak into production builds. Payload enums must not be added until HIR/semantic type conversion can supply and validate their actual field types.
- **Verification:** Focused unit-constructor model tests pass (2 tests), including a raw-attribute regression that calls the public checker with `false` and then the public constructor. It confirms a valid raw marker is not projected as `Unit`, while malformed-argument, empty, and explicit-discriminant fallback cases remain covered. The focused driver projection test and the unaccepted-valid-raw-`@flags` integration regression also pass. `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib --quiet` passes all 80 tests; the equivalent `-p sai_driver --lib --quiet` command passes all 716 tests. `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_ty -p sai_driver` passes.
- **Hostile review:** The initial adversarial review found a P2 public-API bypass: a caller could run `interface_item_check(&hir, false, ...)` for a syntactically valid raw `@flags` enum, then pass that matching check to the unit-enum constructor and receive `Unit`. The constructor now independently inspects raw marker syntax, and the check token binds accepted/raw marker state to the checked enum's variant identity and shape. Regressions exercise the public false-acceptance path directly and through driver collection; they assert the valid raw flags enum is not `Unit` while malformed-argument, empty, and invalid-shape fallback cases remain `Unit`. The same hostile reviewer confirmed the fix and reported no remaining P0–P3 findings.
- **Remaining scope:** Complete the planned semantic type/HIR conversion before payload ADTs; then extend the general local ADT query family-by-family to records, enums, distinct/refined types, and resources. Add imported WIT view ADTs and full `adt_def(DefId)`/`flags_def(DefId)` behavior only when their identity and snapshot boundaries can be represented and tested directly.

### IR-893: add an interned semantic type kernel and conservative HIR conversion

- **Decision:** Add `sai_ty::ty::Ty` and a session-owned, sharded `TyInterner` for primitive types, tuples, and references. Add `lower_ty::lower_ty` for resolved primitive paths without generic arguments, unit/tuple HIR, and `borrow` / `borrow mut`. Signature contexts assign pre-order owner-local region indices; body contexts erase regions; field contexts use the declaration's single implicit region index 0. Keep the result explicit: unsupported HIR and path forms return an `UnsupportedTy` value, without emitting diagnostics or creating a semantic error type.
- **Reason:** IR-892 established that semantic payload enum support depends on a real HIR-to-semantic-type layer. This kernel implements the reusable beginning of docs/impl/03 §§3.5.1–3.5.7 and §3.6.1 without pretending to provide aliases, generic substitution, nominal types, projections, function pointers, or inference. The caller supplies resolved paths from its already owner/snapshot-checked resolution result, avoiding a new untracked query or a second resolution pipeline.
- **Failure boundary:** Arrays, aliases, generic arguments and parameters, `Self`, projections, nominal types, function pointers, inference holes, HIR error types, unresolved/error paths, and wrong-kind paths are unsupported. A borrow in a field without an implicit region parameter is also unsupported. The HIR error marker never becomes an `ErrorGuaranteed` semantic value. A failed conversion poisons its lowering context so callers cannot reuse region numbering after a partially visited type.
- **Review required:** Verify the interner canonicalizes structurally equal types under concurrency, retains handles for its lifetime, and does not let pointer identity become a persisted/query fingerprint. Verify region identities and mutability for nested shared/mutable borrows, sequential signature calls, erased body regions, and field borrows sharing index 0. Verify primitive mapping covers every `PrimTy` except `Array`, and never drops type arguments or treats aliases, nominal definitions, type/const parameters, `Self`, associated projections, test-only results, and wrong-kind paths as primitives. Verify incomplete path segment counts, missing resolutions, and cross-owner HIR fail closed. Verify unsupported or error HIR never manufactures `ErrorGuaranteed`, diagnostics, or successful fallback types. Confirm callers validate the source owner and workspace snapshot before supplying the path map; this type crate cannot validate driver-owned snapshot provenance without creating a dependency cycle.
- **Verification:** `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib` passed all 92 tests, including the field-region regression. The focused lowering tests passed all 8 tests. `cargo check -p sai_ty`, workspace formatting, and `git diff --check` also passed.
- **Hostile review:** The first independent review found that declaration-field borrows needed the single implicit `Sig` region index 0, and that nominal generic arguments needed explicit regression coverage. Commit `21c741d` added a field-specific context with that region rule and a nested/tuple borrow test; commit `30f8127` added the generic nominal argument test. The reviewer reran all 92 tests and found no further actionable blockers. Snapshot freshness remains a caller precondition because the snapshot-bearing driver result lives above `sai_ty` in the crate graph; the implementation docs require that provenance check at integration.
- **Remaining scope:** Integrate the kernel into tracked signature conversion; add static/view regions, `Adt`, generic args and substitution, aliases, `Self`, projections, function pointers, error guarantees, and query fingerprints in separate validated slices. Only then extend payload enum or general ADT conversion.

### IR-894: project supported top-level function signatures

- **Decision:** Add a partial `sai_ty::ty::FnSig` containing ordered input types and an output type. Lower only non-generic, safe, synchronous function HIR without effect or borrow clauses or a `self` parameter, using IR-893's primitive/tuple/reference type kernel. Omitted returns become unit. `FunctionOwnerResolutions::signature_projection(collection, owner)` exposes package-local results, while `signature_projection_with_scopes` also requires the exact source-member and WIT-view closures when those contributed to resolution. The driver lowers types while the same HIR arena and snapshot-bound path map are live. Keep unsupported forms as explicit reasons and emit no diagnostics.
- **Reason:** `impl/03` orders function-signature lowering before general ADTs, and IR-892 makes payload types depend on a reusable type conversion layer. This creates a minimal consumer of IR-893 without changing source acceptance or claiming the complete `fn_sig` query. Safety, async output, ABI, effects, borrow relations, and contract metadata are omitted rather than lost silently.
- **Failure boundary:** Generic and where predicates, unsafe and async signatures, effect and borrow clauses, `self` parameters, unexpected owner kinds, and any unsupported parameter or return type do not produce a `Supported` signature. Errors in path resolution remain errors; unsupported lowering remains a value and never becomes a semantic error type or a diagnostic. Session-local type identity is not used as a stable query fingerprint.
- **Review required:** Confirm that the exposed result is guarded by the exact `Phase1PackageScopesCollection`, every source-member/WIT-view closure used during resolution, and that lowering finishes before its HIR arena is dropped. Confirm the signature model is named/documented as partial and cannot be mistaken for full `fn_sig` or `type_of`; only component `Ty` values are session-interned, omitted return means unit, and parameter order plus signature region order match impl/03 §3.5.2. Confirm generics, where clauses, unsafe/async, effects, borrow clauses, self parameters, external/non-function owner forms, and unsupported HIR paths fail closed without changing existing acceptance or diagnostics. Confirm the `TyInterner` is owned by one `RootDatabase` session and no `Ty` pointer identity reaches persisted fingerprints. Treat unsupported as distinct from semantic error.
- **Remaining scope:** Integrate supported signatures into tracked `fn_sig`/`type_of` queries only after the representation preserves all signature metadata and snapshot inputs. Add nominal types and generic substitution before payload ADTs.
- **Verification:** `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib` passed all 95 tests. `cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 717 tests, including focused package-scope and stale-closure accessor regressions. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --locked --offline -p sai_ty -p sai_driver`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** The first adversarial review found that a package-collection-only accessor could expose projections computed with a different member/WIT closure, and that the implementation docs overstated `FnSig` interning. The package-local accessor now rejects closure-derived results; the scoped accessor checks exact source-member and WIT-view fingerprints, with a mismatched-closure regression. Documentation now says the component types are session-interned. Follow-up review confirmed the fixes and found no remaining actionable issue.

### IR-895: project validated local unit enums into semantic signatures

- **Decision:** Add `TyKind::Adt(DefId)` as the zero-generic-argument nominal identity form. Function-signature lowering accepts an enum path only when the exact definition is present in the same package collection's `LocalInterfaceEnumAdtProjection::Unit` set. Permit fully resolved qualified paths such as `api.State` when every path segment has no explicit generic arguments. Preserve the existing collection and source-member/WIT-view closure guards on the exposed signature projection.
- **Reason:** IR-892 already validates local interface unit enums, while IR-893/894 now provide an interned type representation and a live-HIR signature consumer. This bridges those slices without guessing generic arity or field payloads and without enabling module-level or external nominal types prematurely.
- **Failure boundary:** Valid flags remain represented by the flags projection; payload and generic enums, module-level enums, aliases, external/member/WIT-view definitions, explicit generic arguments, partially resolved paths, and all definitions absent from the unit-enum set remain unsupported. `TyKind::Adt` has no generic-argument payload and is not exposed as general ADT lowering. Type lowering still emits no diagnostics or semantic error types.
- **Review required:** Confirm the zero-argument `Adt(DefId)` identity is sufficient for this slice and that adding generic arguments belongs with the substitution model. Confirm only `Unit` projections from the exact source collection in the owning database session may enter the allowlist, valid flags are excluded, and paths contributed by source-member or WIT-view closures remain unsupported until their owning collection can validate them. Confirm qualified paths are accepted only with complete segment coverage and no explicit arguments, while aliases and other nominal kinds remain closed.
- **Verification:** `mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test -p sai_ty -p sai_driver --locked` passed all 719 driver tests and all 98 `sai_ty` tests, including canonical reuse and distinct `DefId` identity for ADTs, positive/unprovenanced/generic-argument/partial-resolution lowering, and rejection of a collection from another database session. `mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --workspace --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** The first adversarial review found that the package-local shared resolver accepted a collection from another database session, potentially interning its `DefId` values in the wrong database. The shared resolver now checks the session before snapshot and module-tree validation, and a two-database regression covers the rejection. Follow-up review confirmed all public entry points reach the guard (with scoped entry points retaining their earlier guards) and found no remaining actionable issue.

## Sample project decisions

### SR-001: Model distributed order fulfillment as a fixed event-replay saga

- **Decision:** Add `sample/order-fulfillment-saga` as a dependency-free `wasm32-core` library. Replay fixed per-order event arrays through inventory reservation, payment capture, shipment creation, and reverse-order payment-refund/inventory-release compensation. Give each event an order-scoped event ID and each logical step a stable operation key. Keep exact duplicate arrivals in the audit history without applying them twice, and retain partial compensation state as `NeedsReview`.
- **Reason:** Existing examples already cover outbound webhook retry/idempotency and warehouse stock/routing feasibility. This sample focuses on the cross-step transaction lifecycle and the fact that compensation can fail after earlier side effects have committed. Fixed receipts let readers inspect those transitions without pretending the language sample contacts real services.
- **Review required:** Confirm the order-scoped event-ID boundary, unique order IDs within a batch, two-attempt retry budget, reverse compensation order, and treatment of failed or conflicting events as `NeedsReview`. Duplicate order IDs invalidate the batch; the later case's events are retained as rejected arrivals and are never replayed. Confirm that a failed refund keeps both the captured-payment and reserved-inventory facts visible, and that only successful completion of all required compensation yields `Compensated`. The fixtures and test declarations are hand-authored expectations; the current compiler has not run the Stage 3 tests.
- **Verification boundary:** This entry records sample policy decisions, not a production distributed-transaction recommendation. The example has no durable journal, network services, transactional outbox, concurrent event handling, or external side effects. `@derive`, generic array semantics, and `test` execution still require later compiler stages.

### IR-896: project direct local nongeneric records and enums into signatures

- **Decision:** Extend signature lowering's caller-supplied allowlist with only direct `Struct` and `Enum` descriptors from the same `Phase1PackageScopesCollection`. For each descriptor, re-read the owner's source through the collection's snapshot and target configuration, lower the exact current top-level HIR owner, verify owner identity and kind, then admit its `DefId` only when both `generics.params` and `generics.where_preds` are empty. Keep validated interface unit enums in their existing separate allowlist and preserve the IR-895 session/snapshot/collection/closure guards. `TyKind::Adt(DefId)` continues to represent identity only.
- **Reason:** IR-895 established that `Adt(DefId)` is suitable for a zero-argument nominal signature component, while IR-893/894 provide the type kernel and live-HIR consumer. A direct collection descriptor plus current filtered HIR gives this slice positive evidence for local ownership, target visibility, and zero generic arity. The HIR generic list is checked even when a type use omits arguments; syntax at the use site cannot prove the definition is nongeneric. Grouping owner reads by source file avoids re-parsing the current item-tree input for each type in that file.
- **Failure boundary and judgment:** Explicit path arguments continue to return `GenericArguments`. Generic records/enums stay `NominalType` when arguments are omitted; generic definitions with explicit arguments are rejected before the allowlist is consulted. Nonempty where predicates are excluded because they are not represented in `Adt(DefId)`. Since AST generic-parameter iteration filters out parser-recovery `ERROR` children, HIR emptiness alone is insufficient; the driver also rejects recovery nodes and error-marked tokens within each declaration's generic-parameter list and `where` clauses. The regression `type RecoveredRecord<123> { value: Bool }` proves a Struct can survive parser recovery while HIR reports no generic parameters. Aliases are not expanded. Unresolved and target-filtered names have no current collection owner and remain unsupported. Only `collection.scopes.top_level_owners` entries of kind `Struct` or `Enum` are considered, so interface members, source-member closures, dependency packages, and WIT definitions cannot enter the set. If the target-filtered inputs, DefPath, HIR lowering, owner identity, or HIR kind cannot be verified, or relevant generic syntax contains recovery, that definition is omitted from the allowlist without adding a diagnostic. Record fields and enum payload types are not inspected or semantically validated by this signature projection. No general `adt_def`, generic substitution, diagnostics, or source-acceptance changes are added.
- **Review required:** Verify the candidate descriptor source is restricted to the exact current collection and that `current_owner_inputs` plus retained item kinds exclude target-filtered declarations. Confirm the HIR and source-syntax checks jointly prove zero generic parameters and predicates, including recovered nodes and error-marked tokens, without inspecting unrelated field or payload syntax. Confirm a type with omitted use-site arguments but generic HIR remains rejected, explicit arguments remain rejected, and definitions sharing a name keep distinct DefIds. Confirm qualified paths remain supported only when all segments resolve with no arguments and their final DefId belongs to the local allowlist. Confirm aliases, unresolved and target-filtered paths, interface members, dependency/member/WIT definitions, and other nominal families remain closed. Confirm no record field or enum payload semantics, diagnostics, fingerprints, or source acceptance were added. Review the additional per-analysis HIR lowering cost and whether later caching should be introduced without weakening collection provenance.
- **Verification:** `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 720 driver tests and 98 `sai_ty` tests. The focused `function_signature_projection_lowers_only_direct_local_nongeneric_nominals` regression covers record and payload-enum input/output projections, same-named records/enums from distinct package modules, generic records/enums both with omitted and explicit arguments, alias/unresolved/target-filtered/interface-member rejection, and a recovered generic-list case whose HIR lists are empty but whose definition remains outside the allowlist. `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --workspace --locked --offline`, `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `rtk proxy git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** The independent adversarial review found a P2 gap: `GenericParamList::params()` filters out parser-recovery children, so `type Broken<123> { value: U32 }` remains a direct Struct while its HIR generic-parameter vector is empty. The allowlist now checks the exact owner syntax for recovery `ERROR` nodes and error-marked tokens in generic lists and `where` clauses, and the driver regression keeps this malformed Struct unsupported. Follow-up review confirmed the scanner finds the recovered `ERROR` node, the regression proves the resolved type is rejected as `NominalType`, and no other semantic boundary issue remains.

### SR-002: coordinate a fictional privacy request across data stores

- **Decision:** Add `sample/privacy-request-coordinator` as a dependency-free `wasm32-core` library over a fixed seven-row catalog. Require verified identity and confirmed scope before discovery. Require every dependency endpoint to exist in that subject's discovered records; otherwise invalidate the whole plan and apply no receipts. Treat duplicate or zero operation keys as invalid. Replay only matching operation keys and consecutive attempt numbers, with at most two attempts per record. Keep a confirmed deletion state if an extra receipt arrives, while incrementing the receipt-integrity issue count so the request still needs review. Label all topologically unresolved work `DependencyOrderUnresolved`; this may include downstream tasks and does not claim exact cycle membership. An access-only request returns an inventory status, not a disclosure package.
- **Reason:** The user requested additional samples that include more complex projects. This example demonstrates catalog integrity, subject scoping, policy holds, data-lineage prerequisites, bounded retries, result preservation, and partial completion in one reviewable workflow. A fixed receipt fixture exposes those decisions without connecting to personal-data systems or performing deletion.

Confirm dependencies are limited to the discovered subject inventory and that any missing endpoint must stop all actions. Confirm per-record operation keys are stable and unique, attempts are consecutive with a two-attempt teaching budget, extra receipts require review without erasing a confirmed action, and unresolved topological order is reported without asserting exact cycle membership. The fixture does not define real access disclosure, retention, legal, audit-log, or erasure policy.

### IR-897: project unbounded function type parameters into signatures

- **Decision:** Extend only the existing top-level function signature projection with type-only generic binders whose HIR bounds are empty, when the function has no `where` clause and its generic syntax contains no parser-recovery `ERROR` nodes or error-marked tokens. Represent each type use as `TyKind::Param(ParamTy { index, name })`; retain the binder's exact local `DefId` and source order in `FnSig::type_params()`. Resolve a parameter use only through an exact `DefId` lookup in the binder list constructed from the same function's HIR. Require the same `DefPathInterner` to resolve the function and each type parameter, and check that each parameter DefPath is exactly one component below the function with `TypeParam(name)` and disambiguator zero. Keep IR-895's exact session, package collection, snapshot, owner, and closure checks unchanged.
- **Reason:** IR-896 established a source-proven local nominal boundary but left every function with generic binders unsupported. A binder list plus owner-local parameter references is the smallest useful extension that can represent signatures such as `fn identity<T>(value: T) -> T` without requiring generic ADT arguments, substitution, bounds, or a general `adt_def`. Exact binder IDs avoid capturing a same-spelled parameter from another owner, while the source-ordered index supplies a compact structural type representation.
- **Failure boundary and judgment:** Const parameters, bounded type parameters, any `where` clause, recovered generic syntax, foreign or unresolved type-parameter resolutions, explicit generic arguments on ADTs, aliases, and all other unsupported signature types remain unsupported. The driver checks the generic AST because parser recovery can erase malformed generic-list entries from HIR; HIR lowering itself creates parameter DefIds below the exact `source_map.owner().def_id`, and the driver supplies `generics` from the matching top-level function HIR owner. No generic argument lowering, substitution, parameter bounds, member/WIT/dependency ownership, diagnostics, query fingerprints, or source-acceptance changes are included. This deliberately excludes generic methods and other function owner families until they have equivalent collection-bound provenance.
- **Review required:** Confirm that the function owner and exact path-resolution map still come from the current package collection/snapshot, and that only its own HIR type-parameter DefIds lower to `Param`. Verify the DefPath parent check rejects a same-package binder from another function even when both the HIR binder list and resolved type path point to that foreign binder. Verify same-spelled parameters from two functions remain distinct at the binder level, while nested type occurrences use the correct source-ordered indices. Confirm malformed generic syntax cannot turn an empty recovered HIR binder list into a supported signature. Check that bounds, where clauses, const parameters, generic ADT arguments, aliases, wrong-owner parameters, and unsupported signature metadata remain closed, and that failed lowering still poisons the context without changing borrow-region order. Recheck that no member function, dependency, source-member closure, WIT definition, diagnostic, or source syntax acceptance was added.
- **Verification:** `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 720 driver tests and 101 `sai_ty` tests. Focused reruns passed for `function_owner_signature_projection_is_collection_bound_and_conservative` and `foreign_owner_binders_are_rejected_even_with_matching_resolution`. Coverage includes source-ordered binders and nested uses, same-spelled binders with distinct DefIds, wrong-owner resolutions and paired foreign binders, recovered syntax whose HIR binder list is empty, bounds, where clauses, const parameters, generic ADT arguments, aliases, and preserved borrow-region order. `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --workspace --locked --offline`, and `rtk proxy git diff --check` passed.
- **Remaining scope:** Generic ADT argument representation/substitution, bounds and obligation checking, generic aliases, method signatures, non-top-level function owners, query-stable generic type fingerprints, and the complete `fn_sig` query remain separate slices.

### IR-898: project explicit type arguments on region-free local nominals

- **Decision:** Extend only the existing top-level function signature projection to direct local `Struct` and `Enum` applications with explicit type arguments. Build the allowlist from direct descriptors in the exact package collection and snapshot, re-lower each target-filtered owner, verify its HIR owner/kind and exact DefPath provenance, and retain only unbounded type-only parameters with no `where` predicates or recovered declaration syntax. Require exact use-site arity and `GenericArg::Type` for each argument, then lower each argument recursively through the same owner-bound path map. Represent the nominal as `TyKind::Adt(DefId, Arc<[Ty]>)`, ordered by written parameter position, and recursively canonicalize those child `Ty`s through the receiving interner. Continue to allow validated interface unit enums through their separate zero-argument path.
- **Reason:** IR-897 already gives signature lowering owner-bound `ParamTy`s. Structural generic arguments allow direct local types such as `Wrapper<Inner<T>>` to represent that binder without introducing a complete `adt_def`, substitution, or query-stable type identity. The IR-896 representation had no implicit-region slot, so accepting any local nominal without checking its fields could erase the region argument required by spec/07 and shift later borrow indices. The same conservative proof therefore applies to every newly or previously allowed local record/enum.
- **Failure boundary and judgment:** Before admitting any direct local nominal, inspect its full declaration syntax for `ERROR` nodes or error-marked tokens and resolve all field/payload type paths under that exact owner, module scope, package collection, and DefPath context. Accept scalar primitives only from exact `Res::PrimTy` resolutions in the finite allowlist, and accept a type parameter only from an exact `Res::Def(TyParam, DefId)` matching one of that owner's validated binders. Recurse through tuples; function pointers are excluded from the implicit-region parameter rule by spec/07. Reject borrows, `Str`/`Slice`/`SliceMut`, aliases, all nested nominals, nested generic field types, incomplete resolutions, recovered syntax, and unknown shapes. This intentionally rejects some region-free cases rather than solving the spec's whole-program least fixed point. A hostile regression installs an exact local struct `DefId` for a colliding `Bool` path after confirming the ordinary source resolver chooses the prelude primitive; spelling-based recognition would admit that borrow-bearing local type and its wrapper as region-free. This allowlist is shared with IR-906 field projection, where an unvalidated or region-bearing nominal also disables sibling array support. Use-site generic syntax is independently gated across all function parameter and return types, including nested `GenericArgList`s, because HIR currently drops the missing-close marker while retaining a valid-looking prefix. Missing, extra, const, and associated-binding arguments fail closed. These checks add no diagnostics and do not change source acceptance.
- **Review required:** Verify the candidate definitions remain restricted to the current target-filtered collection and exact snapshot, owner, and DefPath interner. Confirm every field/payload path is resolved under its exact owner and module scope; primitive spelling cannot override an exact local `Def` resolution, and only that owner's exact type-parameter `DefId` is accepted. Nested `Wrapper<Inner<T>>` must retain the right binder identity and canonical child type. Confirm arity and kind failures reject before constructing an ADT. Verify declaration-level field recovery and generic-argument recovery (including missing closers and empty `<>`) are found in syntax even when HIR appears valid. Confirm a record field or enum payload containing a borrow, view, alias, or nested nominal cannot be represented without its implicit region parameter, including through a transitive wrapper, and that the same rule covers prior nongeneric candidates. Confirm function-pointer fields are safe to pass by the spec's exclusion; this check is not field-type validation or full nominal region analysis. Recheck that aliases, const arguments, bounds, `where` clauses, interface members, dependencies, source-member/WIT closures, other nominal families, diagnostics, substitution, and query fingerprints remain outside this slice.
- **Verification:** `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib` passed all 103 tests; `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 723 tests. The focused regression `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver function_owner_signature_projection_is_collection_bound_and_conservative --lib` passed, as did the `sai_ty generic_adt` interning tests (2/2). `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --workspace --locked --offline`, `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `rtk proxy git diff --check` passed.
- **Remaining scope:** Full implicit-region fixed-point analysis, resolved type checking for fields/payloads, generic alias expansion, const arguments, bounds and obligation checking, substitution, general ADT definitions, query-stable generic type fingerprints, and the complete `fn_sig` query remain separate slices.

### IR-899 (2026-10-25): project target-bounded literal arrays into function signatures

- **Decision:** Extend the existing top-level function signature projection with structural `TyKind::Array(Ty, u128)`. Accept only a path whose resolved base is the built-in `Res::PrimTy(PrimTy::Array)`, represented by one unqualified path segment with exactly two arguments: an element type followed by a nonnegative integer literal whose HIR value is `Some(u128)`. Require that literal to fit the target pointer width recorded on the exact package collection, lower the element recursively through the existing owner-bound path map, and intern it through the session's `TyInterner`. Keep body and field lowering unchanged.
- **Reason:** The type specification treats `Array<T, N>` as structural, and pointer width determines the range of its `USize` length. Carrying only a checked integer literal makes arrays useful in projected signatures without implementing const evaluation, const-parameter substitution, or the complete generic-argument checker. The built-in resolution identity distinguishes the prelude constructor from a source declaration that shadows `Array`.
- **Failure boundary and judgment:** Reject any alias or shadowed `Array`, qualified/segmented form, absent or additional arguments, wrong argument kinds, boolean/character/negative/parameter/expression constants, integer literals beyond HIR's `u128` representation, target-width overflow, and unknown target width. Associated-type binding entries are excluded from the type/const argument count but rejected as an unsupported argument kind. The driver checks the generic-argument syntax subtree for parser recovery before HIR lowering, including nested and missing-close forms. Only a current top-level function signature projection supplies target width; arrays remain unsupported in body/field contexts and other query paths. No const-generic parameters, general const conversion/evaluation, type substitution, array value checking, or source acceptance changes are included.
- **Review required:** Verify the projection still enforces exact database session, collection, workspace snapshot, function owner, and path-resolution provenance. Confirm the target width is taken from that same collection, with `Array<T, 0>`, the largest representable 32-bit and 64-bit lengths, and the first out-of-range values behaving correctly. Check built-in identity under local shadowing, exact argument order/arity/kinds, that associated bindings do not affect arity but remain rejected, negative and noninteger rejection, `u128` overflow recovery, nested arrays and exact function-binder `ParamTy` preservation, and borrow-region numbering across array elements. Confirm parser recovery cannot turn malformed argument syntax into a supported prefix and the interner recursively canonicalizes array elements from another interner. Recheck that aliases, body/field uses, const params/evaluation, and unrelated projection surfaces remain unsupported.
- **Verification:** `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_ty --lib` passed all 106 tests, and `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo test --locked --offline -p sai_driver --lib` passed all 725 tests. Focused runs passed for `sai_ty built_in_array_types_require_target_fit_nonnegative_integer_lengths`, `sai_driver function_signature_projection_lowers_builtin_arrays_with_target_width_checks`, and `sai_driver function_signature_projection_does_not_treat_a_shadowed_array_name_as_builtin`. Coverage includes zero and 32/64-bit boundaries, too-large HIR integer values, non-integer/negative lengths, argument count and kind, associated-binding rejection, recovered syntax, nested arrays and exact binder identity, borrow-region order, shadowing, and cross-interner canonicalization. `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo check --workspace --locked --offline`, `rtk proxy mise exec rust@stable -- cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `rtk proxy git diff --check` passed.
- **Hostile review:** The independent read-only review found a P2 classification mismatch: a trailing associated binding was counted toward array arity, reporting wrong arity instead of unsupported argument kind. The implementation now excludes bindings from arity and rejects them explicitly; a direct HIR regression covers the exact boundary. Follow-up review confirmed the fix and found no remaining actionable findings.
- **Remaining scope:** Array lengths from const parameters or expressions, const-generic lowering, arrays in bodies/fields/aliases, general array type checking and value checking, the complete `fn_sig`/`type_of` queries, and query-stable type fingerprints remain separate work.

### IR-900 (2026-10-25): project simple local aliases into function signatures

- **Decision:** Extend only the existing top-level function signature projection with values from direct, same-package, top-level type aliases in the exact current package collection. Admit an alias only when its current target-filtered ItemTree and HIR owner agree, its DefPath ends in a zero-disambiguator `TypeNs` component, its AST and HIR have no generic parameters or `where` predicates, and its declaration contains no parser recovery. Lower its right-hand side using the existing signature type-lowering context without an alias allowlist, then reject the result if it contains a reference region anywhere inside tuples, arrays, nominal arguments, or function-pointer inputs and outputs. Pass the resulting `DefId -> Ty` map only to the function signature context.
- **Reason:** The preceding projection can already lower primitives, tuples, literal arrays, and validated local nominals. Reusing those lowering rules makes simple aliases useful without creating a general alias-expansion query or a recursive expansion path.
- **Failure boundary and judgment:** This intentionally supports only aliases whose right-hand sides are accepted directly by existing lowering and contain no alias path. Consequently nested aliases, alias chains, self references and cycles, unsupported or recovered right-hand sides, regions, refined aliases, generic aliases, and aliases outside the current package's direct owner set remain unsupported. The syntax- and HIR-owner checks, current-snapshot `current_owner_inputs`, and exact alias `DefId` lookup fail closed when evidence is absent. Alias generic arguments are rejected even when an explicit empty list is written. This does not add alias-cycle diagnostics, substitution, alias-use tracking, `type_of`, general `fn_sig`, new diagnostics, or source acceptance.

Confirm the RHS is lowered before any alias values are attached, so nested aliases and cycles cannot be traversed, and that the recursive region scan covers tuple, array, ADT, and function-pointer input/output children. Confirm alias values are available only to the exact function-signature context and still flow through the existing collection, snapshot, closure, function-owner and interner guards. The focused driver regression covers direct primitive/tuple/literal-array aliases, repeated alias identity, generic and refined aliases, chains, tuple-nested aliases, cycles, regions, recovered generic syntax, stale collections, and a function-pointer alias composed inside another function pointer; lowerer regressions cover explicit empty arguments, body contexts, unlisted aliases, and external DefIds.
